1.1: The first account I made, O Theophilos, of all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 began both to do and to teach,
1.2: until the day when He was taken up, after giving instructions through the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh to the emissaries whom He had chosen,
1.3: to whom He also presented Himself alive after His suffering by many infallible proofs, being seen by them for forty days, speaking concerning the Malḵuth of Elohim.
1.4: And meeting with them, He commanded them not to leave Yerushalayim, but to wait for the Promise of the Father, “which you have heard from Me -
1.5: because Yoḥanan truly immersed in water, but you shall be immersed in the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh not many days from now.”
1.6: So when they had come together, they asked Him, saying, “Aḏonai, would You at this time restore the Malḵuth to Yisra’ĕl?”
1.7: And He said to them, “It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority.
1.8: “But you shall receive power when the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh has come upon you, and you shall be My witnesses in Yerushalayim, and in all Yahuḏah and Shomeron, and to the end of the earth.”
1.9: And having said this, while they were looking on, He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.
1.10: And as they were gazing into the shamayim as He went up, see, two men stood by them dressed in white,
1.11: who also said, “Men of Galil, why do you stand looking up into the shamayim? This same 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, who was taken up from you into the shamayim, shall come in the same way as you saw Him go into the shamayim.”
1.12: Then they went back to Yerushalayim from the Mount of Olives, which is near Yerushalayim, a Shabbath day’s journey.
1.13: And when they came in, they went up into the upper room where they were staying: both Kĕpha and Ya’aqoḇ and Yoḥanan and Andri, Philippos and T’oma, Bartholomi and Mattithyahu, Ya’aqoḇ of Ḥĕleph and Shim’on ‘the Enthusiast’, and Yahuḏah of Ya’aqoḇ.
1.14: All these were continuing with one mind in prayer and supplication, with the women and Miryam the mother of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and with His brothers.
1.15: And in those days Kĕpha, standing up in the midst of the talmidim - and there was a gathering of about a hundred and twenty - said,
1.16: “Men and brothers, this Scripture had to be filled which the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh spoke before by the mouth of Dawiḏ concerning Yahuḏah, who became a guide to those who seized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏,
1.17: because he was numbered with us and received his share in this service.”
1.18: This one, therefore, purchased a field with the wages of unrighteousness, and falling forward, he burst open in the middle and all his intestines gushed out.
1.19: And it became known to all those dwelling in Yerushalayim, so that in their own language that field was called, Ḥaqal Dema, that is, Field of Blood.
1.20: “For it has been written in the Book of Tehillim, ‘Let his dwelling lie waste, and let no one live in it,’ and, ‘Let another take his office.’
1.21: “It is therefore necessary that of the men who have been with us all the time that the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went in and out among us,
1.22: beginning from the immersion of Yoḥanan to that day when He was taken up from us, that one of these should become a witness with us of His resurrection.”
1.23: And they put forward two: Yosĕph called Barsabba, who was also called Yustos, and Mattithyahu.
1.24: And praying they said, “You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two You have chosen
1.25: to receive the share in this service and office of the emissary from which Yahuḏah by transgression fell, to go to his own place.”
1.26: And they cast their lots, and the lot fell on Mattithyahu. And he was numbered with the eleven emissaries.

10.1: Now there was a certain man in Kaisereia called Kornĕlius, a captain of what was called the Italian Regiment,
10.2: dedicated, and revering Elohim with all his household, doing many kind deeds to the people, and praying to Elohim always.
10.3: He clearly saw in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, a messenger of Elohim coming to him, and saying to him, “Kornĕlius!”
10.4: And looking intently at him, and becoming afraid, he said, “What is it, master?” And he said to him, “Your prayers and your kind deeds have come up for a remembrance before Elohim.
10.5: “And now send men to Yapho, and send for Shim’on who is also called Kĕpha.
10.6: “He is staying with Shim’on, a leather-tanner, whose house is by the sea.”
10.7: And when the messenger who spoke to him went away, Kornĕlius called two of his household servants, and a dedicated soldier from among those who waited on him continually.
10.8: And having explained to them all, he sent them to Yapho.
10.9: And on the next day, as they were on their way and approaching the city, Kĕpha went up on the house-top to pray, about the sixth hour.
10.10: And he became hungry and wanted to eat. But while they were preparing, he fell into a trance,
10.11: and he saw the shamayim opened and a certain vessel like a great sheet bound at the four corners, descending to him and let down to the earth,
10.12: in which were all kinds of four-footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping creatures, and the birds of the shamayim.
10.13: And a voice came to him, “Rise up, Kĕpha, slay and eat.”
10.14: But Kĕpha said, “Not at all, Aḏonai! Because I have never eaten whatever is common or unclean.”
10.15: And a voice came to him again the second time, “What Elohim has cleansed you do not consider common.”
10.16: And this took place three times, and the vessel was taken back to the shamayim.
10.17: And while Kĕpha was doubting within himself about what the vision that he had seen might mean, look, the men who had been sent from Kornĕlius, having asked for the house of Shim’on, stood at the gate,
10.18: and calling out, they enquired whether Shim’on, also known as Kĕpha, was staying there.
10.19: And as Kĕpha was thinking about the vision, the Ruaḥ said to him, “See, three men seek you.
10.20: “But rise up, go down and go with them, not doubting at all, for I have sent them.”
10.21: So Kĕpha went down to the men who had been sent to him from Kornĕlius, and said, “Look, I am the one you seek. Why have you come?”
10.22: And they said, “Kornĕlius the captain, a righteous man and one who reveres Elohim and well spoken of by the entire nation of the Yahuḏim, was instructed by a qodesh messenger to send for you to his house, and to hear words from you.”
10.23: So inviting them in, he housed them. And on the next day Kĕpha went away with them, and some brothers from Yapho went with him.
10.24: And the following day they entered into Kaisereia. And Kornĕlius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
10.25: And it came to be, that when Kĕpha entered, Kornĕlius met him and fell down at his feet and bowed before him.
10.26: But Kĕpha raised him up, saying, “Stand up, I myself am also a man.”
10.27: And talking with him, he went in and found many who had come together.
10.28: And he said to them, “You know that a Yahuḏi is not allowed to associate with, or go to one of another race. But Elohim has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
10.29: “That is why I came without hesitation when I was sent for. So I ask, why have you sent for me?”
10.30: And Kornĕlius said, “Four days ago I was fasting until this hour. And at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and see, a man stood before me in shining garments,
10.31: and said, ‘Kornĕlius, your prayer has been heard, and your kind deeds were remembered before Elohim.
10.32: ‘Now send to Yapho and call Shim’on here, who is also called Kĕpha. He is staying in the house of Shim’on, a leather-tanner, by the sea. When he comes, he shall speak to you.’
10.33: “So I sent to you immediately, and you have done well to come. And now, we are all present before Elohim, to hear all that you have been commanded by Elohim.”
10.34: And opening his mouth, Kĕpha said, “Truly I see that Elohim shows no partiality,
10.35: but in every nation, he who reveres Him and works righteousness is accepted by Him.
10.36: “He sent the Word to the children of Yisra’ĕl, bringing the Good News: peace through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ! He is Aḏon of all.
10.37: “You know what Word came to be throughout all Yahuḏah, beginning from Galil after the immersion which Yoḥanan proclaimed:
10.38: how Elohim anointed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for Elohim was with Him.
10.39: “And we are witnesses of all He did, both in the country of the Yahuḏim and in Yerushalayim, whom they even killed by hanging on a timber.
10.40: “Elohim raised up this One on the third day, and let Him be seen,
10.41: not to all the people, but to witnesses, those having been chosen before by Elohim - to us who ate and drank with Him after He arose from the dead.
10.42: “And He commanded us to proclaim to the people, and to witness that it is He who was appointed by Elohim to be Judge of the living and the dead.
10.43: “To this One all the Neḇi’im bear witness, that through His Name, everyone believing in Him receives forgiveness of sins.”
10.44: While Kĕpha was still speaking these words, the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh fell upon all those hearing the Word.
10.45: And those of the circumcision who believed were astonished, as many as came with Kĕpha, because the gift of the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh had been poured out on the gentiles also,
10.46: for they were hearing them speaking with tongues and extolling Elohim. Then Kĕpha answered,
10.47: “Is anyone able to forbid water, that these should not be immersed who have received the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh - even as also we?”
10.48: And he commanded them to be immersed in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ. Then they asked him to remain a few days.

11.1: And the emissaries and brothers who were in Yahuḏah heard that the gentiles also received the Word of Elohim.
11.2: And when Kĕpha went up to Yerushalayim, those of the circumcision were contending with him,
11.3: saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them!”
11.4: But Kĕpha began and laid it forth to them in order, saying:
11.5: “I was in the city of Yapho praying. And in a trance I saw a vision, a certain vessel descending like a great sheet, let down from the shamayim by four corners, and it came to me.
11.6: “Having looked into it, I perceived and I saw four-footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping creatures, and the birds of the shamayim.
11.7: “And I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise up, Kĕpha, slay and eat.’
11.8: “But I said, ‘Not at all, Aḏonai! Because whatever is common or unclean has never entered into my mouth.’
11.9: “And the voice answered me again from the shamayim, ‘What Elohim has cleansed you do not consider common.’
11.10: “And this took place three times, and all were drawn up again into the shamayim.
11.11: “And see, immediately three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent to me from Kaisereia.
11.12: “And the Ruaḥ said to me to go with them, not doubting at all. And these six brothers also went with me, and we went into the man’s house.
11.13: “And he told us how he had seen a messenger standing in his house, who said to him, ‘Send men to Yapho, and call for Shim’on who is also called Kĕpha,
11.14: who shall speak to you words, by which you shall be saved, you and all your house.’
11.15: “And as I began to speak, the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh fell upon them, as upon us at the beginning.
11.16: “And I remembered the word of the Aḏon, how He said, ‘Yoḥanan indeed immersed in water, but you shall be immersed in the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.’
11.17: “So if Elohim gave them the same gift as He gave us when we believed on the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, how was I able to withstand Elohim?”
11.18: And having heard this, they were silent, and praised Elohim, saying, “Then Elohim has indeed also given to the gentiles repentance to ḥai.”
11.19: Then, indeed, they who were scattered because of the pressure that arose over Stephanos passed through to Phoinikĕ, and Kupros, and Antioḵeia, speaking the Word to no one except the Yahuḏim only.
11.20: But some of them were men from Kupros and Kurĕnĕ, who, when they had come to Antioḵeia, spoke to the Yawanites, bringing the Good News: the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏!
11.21: And the hand of the Aḏon was with them, and a great number having believed turned to the Aḏon.
11.22: And Word of it came to the ears of the assembly in Yerushalayim, and they sent out Barnaḇah to go as far as Antioḵeia,
11.23: who, having come, and seeing the favor of Elohim, was glad, and encouraged them all with purpose of heart to cling to the Aḏon.
11.24: Because he was a good man, and filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh and with belief. And large numbers were added to the Aḏon.
11.25: Then Barnaḇah went to Tarsos to seek Sha’ul,
11.26: and having found him, he brought him to Antioḵeia. And it came to be that for an entire year they came together in the assembly and taught large numbers. And the talmidim were called ‘Mashiaḥiyim’ first in Antioḵeia.
11.27: And in those days neḇi’im came from Yerushalayim to Antioḵeia.
11.28: And one of them, named Ḥaḡaḇ, stood up and indicated by the Ruaḥ that there was going to be a great scarcity of food over all the world - which also took place under Klaudius Kaisar.
11.29: So the talmidim, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers dwelling in Yahuḏah.
11.30: This they also did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnaḇah and Sha’ul.

12.1: And about that time Hĕrodĕs the meleḵ put forth his hands to do evil to some from the assembly.
12.2: And he killed Ya’aqoḇ the brother of Yoḥanan with the sword.
12.3: And seeing that it was pleasing to the Yahuḏim, he proceeded further to arrest Kĕpha as well - and they were the Days of Matstsoth.
12.4: So when he had seized him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four squads of soldiers to watch over him, intending to bring him before the people after Pesaḥ.
12.5: So Kĕpha was indeed kept in prison, but prayer was earnestly made to Elohim on his behalf by the assembly.
12.6: And when Hĕrodĕs was about to bring him out, that night Kĕpha was sleeping, bound with two chains between two soldiers. And the guards before the door were keeping the prison.
12.7: And see, a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 stood by, and a light shone in the building. And smiting the side of Kĕpha he raised him up, saying, “Get up quickly!” And his chains fell off his hands.
12.8: And the messenger said to him, “Gird yourself and bind on your sandals,” and he did so. And he said to him, “Put on your garment and follow me.”
12.9: And coming out he followed him, and knew not that what was done by the messenger was true, but thought he was seeing a vision.
12.10: And when they had passed the first and the second guard posts, they came to the iron gate that leads to the city, which opened to them by itself. And they went out and went down one street, and the messenger instantly withdrew from him.
12.11: And when Kĕpha had come to himself, he said, “Now I truly know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent His messenger, and delivered me from the hand of Hĕrodĕs and all the anticipation of the Yahuḏim.”
12.12: And having realized this, he went to the house of Miryam, the mother of Yoḥanan who was also called Markos, where many were gathered together and were praying.
12.13: And when Kĕpha knocked at the door of the gate, a girl named Rhodĕ came to answer.
12.14: And when she recognized Kĕpha’s voice, she did not open the gate because of her joy, but ran in and reported that Kĕpha stood before the gate.
12.15: And they said to her, “You are mad!” But she kept insisting that it was so, and they said, “It is his messenger.”
12.16: And Kĕpha continued knocking, and having opened they saw him and were amazed.
12.17: And motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he told them how the Aḏon brought him out of the prison. And he said, “Report this to Ya’aqoḇ and to the brothers.” And he left and went to another place.
12.18: Now when day came, there was no small stir among the soldiers about what had become of Kĕpha.
12.19: And when Hĕrodĕs had searched for him and did not find him, he examined the guards and ordered them to be led away. And he went down from Yahuḏah to Kaisereia, and stayed there.
12.20: Now Hĕrodĕs had been highly displeased with the people of Tsor and Tsiḏon, but with one mind they came to him, and having made Blastos the meleḵ’s chamberlain their friend, they were asking for peace, because their country was supplied with food from the meleḵ’s country.
12.21: And on an appointed day Hĕrodĕs, having put on his royal clothes, sat on his throne and gave an address to them.
12.22: And the people kept shouting, “The voice of a mighty one and not of a man!”
12.23: And instantly a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smote him, because he did not give the esteem to Elohim. And becoming worm-eaten, he died.
12.24: And the Word of Elohim went on growing and spreading.
12.25: And Barnaḇah and Sha’ul returned from Yerushalayim, having completed the service, and having taken with them Yoḥanan who was also called Markos.

13.1: And in the assembly that was at Antioḵeia there were certain neḇi’im and teachers: both Barnaḇah and Shim’on who was called Niger, and Lukios of Kurĕnĕ, and Manaḥĕm who had been brought up with Hĕrodĕs the district ruler, and Sha’ul.
13.2: And as they were doing service to the Aḏon and fasted, the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh said, “Separate unto Me Barnaḇah and Sha’ul for the work to which I have called them.”
13.3: Then having fasted and prayed, and having laid hands on them, they sent them away.
13.4: So they, having been sent out by the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, went down to Seleukeia, and from there they sailed to Kupros.
13.5: And having come into Salamis, they proclaimed the Word of Elohim in the congregations of the Yahuḏim. And they also had Yoḥanan as an attendant.
13.6: And having passed through all the island to Paphos, they found a certain magician, a false prophet, a Yahuḏi whose name was Bar-Yahoshua,
13.7: who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. This man, having called for Barnaḇah and Sha’ul, earnestly sought to hear the Word of Elohim.
13.8: But Elumas the magician - for so his name is translated - withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the belief.
13.9: Then Sha’ul, also called Paulus, filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, looked intently at him,
13.10: and said, “O son of the devil, filled with all deceit and all recklessness, you enemy of all righteousness, shall you not cease corrupting the straight Ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
13.11: “And now, see, the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is upon you, and you shall be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.” And instantly a dark mist fell on him, and he went around seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
13.12: And having seen what took place, the proconsul believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Aḏon.
13.13: And having put out from Paphos, Sha’ul and those with him came to Pergĕ in Pamphulia. And Yoḥanan, having left them, returned to Yerushalayim.
13.14: But passing through from Pergĕ, they came to Antioḵeia in Pisidia, and went into the congregation on the Shabbath day and sat down.
13.15: And after the reading of the Torah and the Neḇi’im, the rulers of the congregation sent to them, saying, “Men, brothers, if you have any word of encouragement for the people, speak.”
13.16: And Sha’ul, standing up and motioning with his hand said, “Men, Yisra’ĕlites, and those revering Elohim, listen:
13.17: “The Elohim of this people Yisra’ĕl chose our fathers, and exalted the people in their sojourning in the land of Mitsrayim, and with a high arm He brought them out of it.
13.18: “Now for a time of about forty years He sustained them in the wilderness.
13.19: “And having destroyed seven nations in the land of Kena’an, He gave their land to them as an inheritance.
13.20: “And after that He gave judges for about four hundred and fifty years, until Shemu’ĕl the naḇi.
13.21: “But then they asked for a meleḵ, and Elohim gave them Sha’ul the son of Qish, a man of the tribe of Binyamin, for forty years.
13.22: “And having removed him, He raised up for them Dawiḏ as meleḵ, to whom also He gave witness and said, ‘I have found Dawiḏ the son of Yishai, a man after My own heart, who shall do all My desires.’
13.23: “From this one’s seed, according to the promise, Elohim raised up for Yisra’ĕl a Savior, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏,
13.24: after Yoḥanan had first proclaimed the immersion of repentance to all the people of Yisra’ĕl, before His coming.
13.25: “And as Yoḥanan was completing his mission, he said, ‘Who do you suppose I am? I am not He. But see, there comes One after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to loose.’
13.26: “Men, brothers, sons of the race of Aḇraham, and those among you revering Elohim, to you the Word of this deliverance has been sent,
13.27: for those dwelling in Yerushalayim, and their rulers, because they did not know Him, nor even the voices of the Neḇi’im which are read every Shabbath, have filled them in having judged Him.
13.28: “And having found not one cause for death, they asked Pilatus that He should be put to death.
13.29: “And when they had accomplished all that was written concerning Him, taking Him down from the timber, they laid Him in a tomb.
13.30: “But Elohim raised Him from the dead,
13.31: and He was seen for many days by those who came up with Him from Galil to Yerushalayim, who are His witnesses to the people.
13.32: “And we bring you the Good News, the promise made to the fathers,
13.33: that Elohim has filled this for us, their children, having raised up 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, as it has also been written in the second Tehillah, ‘You are My Bĕn, today I have brought You forth.’
13.34: “And that He raised Him out of the dead, no more to return to corruption, He has said thus, ‘I shall give you the trustworthy kindnesses of Dawiḏ.’
13.35: “For this reason He also says in another Tehillah, ‘You shall not give Your Kind One to see corruption.’
13.36: “For Dawiḏ, indeed, having served his own generation by the counsel of Elohim, fell asleep, was buried with his fathers, and saw corruption,
13.37: but He whom Elohim raised up saw no corruption.
13.38: “Let it therefore be known to you, brothers, that through this One forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you,
13.39: and by Him everyone who believes is declared right from all of which you were not able to be declared right by the Torah of Mosheh.
13.40: “Watch then that what was said in the Neḇi’im does not come upon you:
13.41: “See, you despisers, marvel and perish, for I work a work in your days, a work which you would in no way believe if someone were to declare it to you.’ ”
13.42: And when the Yahuḏim went out of the congregation, the gentiles begged to have these words spoken to them the next Shabbath.
13.43: And when the congregation had broken up, many of the Yahuḏim and of the worshipping converts followed Sha’ul and Barnaḇah, who, speaking to them, were urging them to continue in the favor of Elohim.
13.44: And on the next Shabbath almost all the city came together to hear the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
13.45: But when the Yahuḏim saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy. And contradicting and speaking evil, they opposed what Sha’ul was saying.
13.46: But speaking boldly, Sha’ul and Barnaḇah said, “It was necessary that the Word of Elohim should be spoken to you first, but since you thrust it away, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting ḥai, see, we turn to the gentiles.
13.47: “For so the Aḏon has commanded us, ‘I have appointed you to be a light to the gentiles, that you should be for deliverance to the ends of the earth.’ ”
13.48: And when the gentiles heard this, they were glad and praised the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And as many as had been appointed to everlasting ḥai believed.
13.49: And the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was being spread throughout the entire country.
13.50: But the Yahuḏim stirred up the worshipping and noble women and the chief men of the city, and raised up persecution against Sha’ul and Barnaḇah, and threw them out of their borders.
13.51: And shaking off the dust from their feet against them, they came to Ikonion.
13.52: And the talmidim were filled with joy and the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.

14.1: And it came to be in Ikonion that they went together into the congregation of the Yahuḏim, and spoke in such a way that a great number of both Yahuḏim and Yawanites believed.
14.2: But the Yahuḏim who would not obey stirred up the gentiles and evilly influenced their beings against the brothers.
14.3: So they remained a long time, speaking boldly in the Aḏon, who was bearing witness to the Word of His favor, giving signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
14.4: And the crowd of the city was divided, and some sided with the Yahuḏim, and some with the emissaries.
14.5: But when a move took place by both the gentiles and Yahuḏim, with their rulers, to mistreat and stone them,
14.6: they became aware of it and fled to Lustra and Derbĕ, cities of Lukaonia, and the country round about.
14.7: And they were bringing the Good News there.
14.8: And in Lustra there was sitting a certain man, disabled in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who had never walked.
14.9: This one heard Sha’ul speaking, who, looking intently at him and seeing that he had belief to be healed,
14.10: said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” And he sprang up and began to walk.
14.11: And when the crowds saw what Sha’ul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in Lukaonian, “The mighty ones have become like men and come down to us!”
14.12: And they called Barnaḇah - Zeus, and Sha’ul - Hermĕs, since he was the chief speaker.
14.13: And the priest of Zeus, whose temple was in front of their city, brought oxen and wreaths to the gates, and wanted to offer with the crowds.
14.14: And when the emissaries Barnaḇah and Sha’ul heard this, they tore their garments and ran in among the crowd, crying out
14.15: and saying, “Men, why are you doing this? We also are men with the same nature as you, bringing to you the Good News: to turn from these worthless matters to the living Elohim, who made the shamayim, and the earth, and the sea, and all that is in them,
14.16: who in past generations allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways,
14.17: though, indeed, He did not leave Himself without witness, doing good - giving us rain from the shamayim and fruit-bearing seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”
14.18: Even with these words they still had difficulty in stopping the crowds from offering to them.
14.19: But Yahuḏim arrived from Antioḵeia and Ikonion, and having won over the crowds, they stoned Sha’ul, dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
14.20: But while the talmidim gathered around him, he rose up and went into the city. And on the next day he went away with Barnaḇah to Derbĕ.
14.21: And having brought the Good News to that city, and having instructed many, they returned to Lustra, and Ikonion, and Antioḵeia,
14.22: strengthening the beings of the talmidim, encouraging them to continue in the belief, and that through many pressures we have to enter the Malḵuth of Elohim.
14.23: And having appointed elders in every assembly, having prayed with fasting, they committed them to the Aḏon in whom they had believed.
14.24: And having passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphulia.
14.25: And having spoken the Word in Pergĕ, they went down to Attaleia,
14.26: and from there they sailed to Antioḵeia, where they had been committed to the favor of Elohim for the work which they had completed.
14.27: And having arrived, and having gathered together the assembly, they related all that Elohim had done with them, and that He had opened the door of belief to the gentiles.
14.28: And they remained there a long time with the talmidim.

15.1: And certain men came down from Yahuḏah and were teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised, according to the practice of Mosheh, you are unable to be saved.”
15.2: So when Sha’ul and Barnaḇah had no small dissension and dispute with them, they arranged for Sha’ul and Barnaḇah and certain others of them to go up to Yerushalayim, to the emissaries and elders, about this question.
15.3: So, being sent on their way by the assembly, they passed through Phoinikĕ and Shomeron, relating the conversion of the gentiles. And they were causing great joy to all the brothers.
15.4: And having arrived in Yerushalayim, they were received by the assembly and the emissaries and the elders. And they reported all that Elohim had done with them.
15.5: And some of the believers who belonged to the sect of the Pharisees, rose up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the Torah of Mosheh.”
15.6: And the emissaries and elders came together to look into this matter.
15.7: And when there had been much dispute, Kĕpha rose up and said to them, “Men, brothers, you know that a good while ago Elohim chose among us, that by my mouth the gentiles should hear the Word of the Good News and believe.
15.8: “And Elohim, who knows the heart, bore witness to them, by giving them the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, as also to us,
15.9: and made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by belief.
15.10: “Now then, why do you try Elohim by putting a yoke on the neck of the talmidim which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
15.11: “But through the favor of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ we trust to be saved, in the same way as they.”
15.12: And all the crowd was silent and were listening to Barnaḇah and Sha’ul declaring how many miracles and wonders Elohim did among the gentiles, through them.
15.13: And after they were silent, Ya’aqoḇ answered, saying, “Men, brothers, listen to me:
15.14: “Shim’on has declared how Elohim first visited the gentiles to take out of them a people for His Name.
15.15: “And the words of the Neḇi’im agree with this, as it has been written:
15.16: ‘After this I shall return and rebuild the Booth of Dawiḏ which has fallen down. And I shall rebuild its ruins, and I shall straighten it,
15.17: so that the remnant of mankind shall seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even all the gentiles on whom My Name has been called, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is doing all this,’
15.18: who has made this known from of old.
15.19: “Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from among the gentiles who are turning to Elohim,
15.20: but that we write to them to abstain from the defilements of idols, and from whoring, and from what is strangled, and from blood.
15.21: “For from ancient generations Mosheh has, in every city, those proclaiming him - being read in the congregations every Shabbath.”
15.22: Then it seemed good to the emissaries and elders, with all the assembly, to send chosen men from among them to Antioḵeia with Sha’ul and Barnaḇah: Yahuḏah being called Barsabba, and Sila, leading men among the brothers,
15.23: having written by their hand this: The emissaries and the elders and the brothers, To the brothers who are of the gentiles in Antioḵeia, and Suria, and Kilikia: Greetings.
15.24: Since we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your lives, to whom we gave no command -
15.25: it seemed good to us, having become of one mind, to send chosen men to you with our beloved Barnaḇah and Sha’ul,
15.26: men who have given up their lives for the Name of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
15.27: We have therefore sent Yahuḏah and Sila, who are also confirming this by word of mouth.
15.28: For it seemed good to the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessities:
15.29: that you abstain from what is offered to idols, and blood, and what is strangled, and whoring. If you keep yourselves from these, you shall do well. Be strong!
15.30: They, therefore, being sent off, went to Antioḵeia. And having gathered the crowd together, they delivered the letter.
15.31: And having read it, they rejoiced over its encouragement.
15.32: And Yahuḏah and Sila, being themselves also neḇi’im, encouraged the brothers with many words and strengthened them.
15.33: And having spent some time, they were sent back in peace from the brothers to the emissaries.
15.34: But it seemed good to Sila to remain.
15.35: And Sha’ul and Barnaḇah continued in Antioḵeia, teaching and bringing, with many others also, the Good News: the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
15.36: And after some days Sha’ul said to Barnaḇah, “Let us now go back and visit our brothers in every city where we proclaimed the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and see how they are.”
15.37: And Barnaḇah purposed to take with them Yoḥanan called Markos.
15.38: But Sha’ul thought it not fit to take with them the one who withdrew from them in Pamphulia, and had not gone with them to the work.
15.39: A sharp feeling therefore came to be, so that they parted from one another. And so Barnaḇah took Markos and sailed to Kupros.
15.40: And Sha’ul chose Sila and went off, being committed by the brothers to the favor of Elohim.
15.41: And he went through Suria and Kilikia, strengthening the assemblies.

16.1: And he came to Derbĕ and Lustra. And see, a certain talmid was there, named Timotiyos, the son of a certain Yahuḏi woman who believed - but his father was Yawanite -
16.2: who was well spoken of by the brothers who were at Lustra and Ikonion.
16.3: Sha’ul wanted to have this one go with him. And he took him and circumcised him because of the Yahuḏim who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was Yawanite.
16.4: And as they went through the cities, they delivered to them the regulations to keep, which were decided by the emissaries and elders at Yerushalayim.
16.5: Then, indeed, the assemblies were strengthened in the belief, and increased in number every day.
16.6: And having passed through Phrugia and the Galatian country, they were forbidden by the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh to speak the Word in Asia.
16.7: When they came to Musia, they tried to go into Bithunia, but the Ruaḥ did not allow them.
16.8: And having passed by Musia, they came down to Troas.
16.9: And in the night a vision appeared to Sha’ul: A man of Makedonia was standing, begging him and saying, “Come over to Makedonia and help us.”
16.10: And when he saw the vision, immediately we sought to go to Makedonia, concluding that the Aḏon had called us to bring the Good News to them.
16.11: Therefore, sailing from Troas, we ran a straight course to Samothrakĕ, and the next day came to Neapolis,
16.12: and from there to Philippi, which is the principal city of that part of Makedonia, a colony. And we were staying in that city for some days.
16.13: And on the Shabbath we went outside the city by a river, where there used to be prayer. And having sat down we were speaking to the women who met there.
16.14: And a certain woman named Ludia, a seller of purple from the city of Thuatira, worshipping Elohim, was hearing, whose heart the Aḏon opened to pay attention to what Sha’ul said.
16.15: And when she was immersed, and her household, she begged us, saying, “If you have judged me to be believing in the Aḏon, come to my house and stay.” And she urged us.
16.16: And it came to be, as we went to prayer, that a certain slave girl possessed with a spirit of Puthon, met us, who brought her masters much profit by foretelling.
16.17: Having followed Sha’ul and us, she cried out, saying, “These men are the servants of the Most High Elohim, who proclaim to us the Way of deliverance.”
16.18: And she was doing this for many days. But Sha’ul, greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ to come out of her.” And it came out that same hour.
16.19: But when her masters saw that their anticipation of money-making was gone, they seized Sha’ul and Sila and dragged them into the market-place to the rulers.
16.20: And having brought them to the magistrates, they said, “These men, being Yahuḏim, greatly disturb our city,
16.21: and they proclaim practices which are not right for us to receive nor to do, being Romans.”
16.22: And the crowd rose up together against them. And the magistrates tore off their garments and commanded them to be beaten with rods.
16.23: And having laid many blows upon them, they threw them into prison, commanding the jailer to keep them safely,
16.24: who, having received such a command, put them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
16.25: And at midnight Sha’ul and Sila were praying and singing songs to Elohim, and the prisoners were listening to them.
16.26: And suddenly a great earthquake took place, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened and all the chains came loose.
16.27: And the jailer, awaking from sleep and seeing the prison doors open, thinking the prisoners had fled, drew his sword and was about to kill himself.
16.28: But Sha’ul called with a loud voice, saying, “Do no harm to yourself, for we are all here.”
16.29: And asking for a light, he ran in, and fell down trembling before Sha’ul and Sila.
16.30: And having led them outside he said, “Masters, what do I have to do to be saved?”
16.31: And they said, “Believe on the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, and you shall be saved, you and your household.”
16.32: And they spoke the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to him and to all who were in his house.
16.33: And taking them in that hour of the night, he washed their wounds, and immediately he was immersed, he and all that were his.
16.34: And having brought them into his house, he put food before them. And he rejoiced with all his household, having believed in Elohim.
16.35: And when day came, the authorities sent the officers, saying, “Let these men go.”
16.36: And the jailer reported these words to Sha’ul, saying, “The captains have sent to let you go. Now then, come out and go in peace.”
16.37: But Sha’ul said to them, “They have beaten us publicly, uncondemned, being Romans. They have thrown us into prison, and now, do they throw us out secretly? No indeed! Let them come themselves and bring us out.”
16.38: And the officers reported these words to the authorities, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans.
16.39: And having come, they pleaded with them and brought them out, and asked them to leave the city.
16.40: So coming out of the prison they went to Ludia, and seeing the brothers, they encouraged them, and went forth.

17.1: And having passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonikĕ, where there was a congregation of the Yahuḏim.
17.2: And according to his practice, Sha’ul went in unto them, and for three Shabbathoth was reasoning with them from the Scriptures,
17.3: explaining and pointing out that ha’Mashiaḥ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and that, “This is ha’Mashiaḥ, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, whom I proclaim to you.”
17.4: And some of them believed, and a large number of the worshipping Yawanites, and not a few of the leading women, joined Sha’ul and Sila.
17.5: But the Yahuḏim who did not believe, having become envious, took some of the wicked men from the market-place, and gathering a mob, disturbed all the city and came upon the house of Yason, and were seeking to bring them out to the people.
17.6: But not finding them, they dragged Yason and some of the brothers to the city rulers, crying out, “They who have turned the world upside down have come here too,
17.7: whom Yason has received. And all of them are acting contrary to the dogmas of Kaisar, saying there is another meleḵ, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.”
17.8: And they troubled the crowd and the city rulers when they heard this.
17.9: And when they had received a pledge from Yason and the rest, they let them go.
17.10: And the brothers immediately sent Sha’ul and Sila away by night to Beroia, who, having come, went into the congregation of the Yahuḏim.
17.11: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonikĕ, who received the Word with great eagerness, and searched the Scriptures daily, if these were so.
17.12: Then many of them truly believed, and also not a few of the Yawanites, decent women as well as men.
17.13: And when the Yahuḏim from Thessalonikĕ came to know that the Word of Elohim was proclaimed by Sha’ul at Beroia, they came there also and stirred up the crowds.
17.14: And then immediately the brothers sent Sha’ul away, to go to the sea, but both Sila and Timotiyos stayed there.
17.15: And those who escorted Sha’ul brought him to Athĕnai. And receiving a command for Sila and Timotiyos to join him as soon as possible, they departed.
17.16: But while Sha’ul was waiting for them at Athĕnai, his spirit was stirred up within him when he saw that the city was utterly idolatrous.
17.17: Therefore, indeed, he was reasoning in the congregation with the Yahuḏim and with the gentile worshippers, and in the market-place daily with those who met there.
17.18: And some of the Epikurean and Stoic philosophers encountered him. And some were saying, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be a proclaimer of strange mighty ones” - because to them he brought the Good News: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and the resurrection!
17.19: So they laid hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “Are we able to know what this fresh teaching is of which you speak?
17.20: “For you are bringing some strangeness to our ears. We want, then, to know what these mean.”
17.21: For all the Athĕnians and the strangers living there spent their leisure time in doing naught but to speak or to hear what is fresh.
17.22: And having stood in the midst of the Areopagus Sha’ul said, “Men of Athĕnai, I see that you are very religious in all.
17.23: “For passing through and observing the objects of your worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO THE UNKNOWN MIGHTY ONE. Not knowing then whom you worship, I make Him known to you:
17.24: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who made the world and all that is in it, this One being Aḏon of the shamayim and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands.
17.25: “Nor is He served with men’s hands - as if needing any - Himself giving to all ḥai, and breath, and all.
17.26: “And He has made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, having ordained beforehand the times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
17.27: to seek the Aḏon, if at least they would reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
17.28: “For in Him we live and move and are, as also some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also His offspring.’
17.29: “Now then, since we are the offspring of Elohim, we should not think that the Elohim is like gold or silver or stone, an image made by the skill and thought of man.
17.30: “Truly, then, having overlooked these times of ignorance, Elohim now commands all men everywhere to repent,
17.31: because He has appointed a day on which He is going to judge the world in righteousness by a Man whom He has appointed, having given proof of this to all by raising Him from the dead.”
17.32: And hearing of the resurrection of the dead, some indeed mocked, while others said, “We shall hear you again concerning this.”
17.33: And so Sha’ul went out from among them.
17.34: But some men joined him and believed, among them Dionusios the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

18.1: And after this Sha’ul left Athĕnai and went to Korinthos.
18.2: And he found a certain Yahuḏi named Aqulas, born in Pontus, who had recently come from Italia with his wife Priskilla - because Klaudius had commanded all the Yahuḏim to leave Rome - and he came to them.
18.3: And because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and was working, for they were tentmakers by trade.
18.4: And he was reasoning in the congregation every Shabbath, and won over both Yahuḏim and Yawanites.
18.5: And when Sila and Timotiyos came down from Makedonia, Sha’ul was pressed by the Ruaḥ, and earnestly witnessed to the Yahuḏim that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 is ha’Mashiaḥ.
18.6: However, when they resisted and blasphemed, he shook his garments and said to them, “Your blood is upon your head, I am clean. From now on I shall go to the gentiles.”
18.7: And having left there he came to the house of a certain man named Yustos, who worshipped Elohim, whose house was next to the congregation.
18.8: And Krispus, the ruler of the congregation, believed in the Aḏon with all his household. And many of the Korinthians, hearing, believed and were immersed.
18.9: And the Aḏon spoke to Sha’ul in the night by a vision, “Do not be afraid, but speak, and do not be silent,
18.10: because I am with you, and no one shall attack you to do you evil, because I have much people in this city.”
18.11: And he remained a year and six months, teaching the Word of Elohim among them.
18.12: And when Gallion was proconsul of Aḵaia, the Yahuḏim with one mind rose up against Sha’ul and brought him to the judgment seat,
18.13: saying, “This one seduces men to worship Elohim contrary to the Torah.”
18.14: And as Sha’ul was about to open his mouth, Gallion said to the Yahuḏim, “If it were a matter of wrongdoing or wicked recklessness, O Yahuḏim, there would be reason why I should bear with you.
18.15: “But if it is a question of words and names and a law which is among you, see to it yourselves, for I do not want to be a judge of these.”
18.16: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
18.17: And all the Yawanites took Sosthenĕs, the ruler of the congregation, and beat him before the judgment seat. But Gallion showed no concern whatever.
18.18: And Sha’ul, having stayed several days more, having taken leave of the brothers, was sailing for Suria, and Priskilla and Aqulas were with him, having shaved his hair at Kengḵreai, for he had taken a vow.
18.19: And he came to Ephesos, and left them there, but he himself went into the congregation and reasoned with the Yahuḏim.
18.20: And when they asked him to stay a longer time with them, he declined,
18.21: but took leave of them, saying, “I have to keep this coming Festival in Yerushalayim by all means, but I shall come back to you, Elohim desiring so.” And he sailed from Ephesos.
18.22: And having come to Kaisereia, going up and greeting the assembly, he went down to Antioḵeia.
18.23: And having spent some time there, he went forth, passing through the country of Galatia and on through Phrugia, strengthening all the talmidim.
18.24: And a certain Yahuḏi named Apollos, born at Alexandria, a learned man and mighty in the Scriptures, came to Ephesos.
18.25: This one had been instructed in the Way of the Aḏon. And being fervent in spirit, he was speaking and teaching that about the Aḏon exactly, though he knew only the immersion of Yoḥanan.
18.26: And he began to speak boldly in the congregation. And when Aqulas and Priskilla heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the Way of Elohim more exactly.
18.27: And when he intended to pass through to Aḵaia, the brothers, having encouraged him, wrote to the talmidim to receive him, who, having arrived, greatly helped those who believed through favor,
18.28: for with power he refuted the Yahuḏim publicly, showing from the Scriptures that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 is ha’Mashiaḥ.

19.1: And it came to be, while Apollos was at Korinthos, that Sha’ul, having passed through the upper parts, came to Ephesos. And having found some talmidim,
19.2: he said to them, “Did you receive the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh when you believed?” And they said to him, “No, we have not even heard that there is a Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.”
19.3: And he said to them, “Into what then were you immersed?” And they said, “Into Yoḥanan’s immersion.”
19.4: And Sha’ul said, “Yoḥanan indeed immersed with an immersion of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the One who is coming after him, that is, in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.”
19.5: And when they heard this, they were immersed in the Name of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
19.6: And when Sha’ul had laid hands on them, the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and naḇu.
19.7: And all the men were about twelve.
19.8: And having gone into the congregation he spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the Malḵuth of Elohim.
19.9: But when some were hardened and did not believe, speaking evil of the Way before the crowd, he withdrew from them and separated the talmidim, reasoning daily in the school of Turannos.
19.10: And this took place for two years, so that all who dwelt in Asia heard the Word of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, both Yahuḏim and Yawanites.
19.11: And Elohim worked unusual miracles through the hands of Sha’ul,
19.12: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were brought from his body to the sick, and the diseases left them and the wicked spirits went out of them.
19.13: But certain roving Yahuḏi exorcists took it upon themselves to call the Name of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 over those who had wicked spirits, saying, “We adjure you by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 whom Sha’ul proclaims.”
19.14: And there were seven sons of a certain Skeua, a Yahuḏi chief kohĕn, who were doing this.
19.15: And the wicked spirit answering, said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 I know, and Sha’ul I know, but who are you?”
19.16: And the man in whom the wicked spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
19.17: And this became known to all, both Yahuḏim and Yawanites dwelling in Ephesos. And fear fell on them all, and the Name of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was made great.
19.18: And many who had believed came confessing and declaring their deeds.
19.19: And many of those who had practiced magic brought their books together, burning them before all. And they reckoned up the value of them, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
19.20: So the Word of the Aḏon was growing mightily and prevailing.
19.21: Now when these had been completed, Sha’ul purposed in the Ruaḥ, when he had passed through Makedonia and Aḵaia, to go to Yerushalayim, saying, “After I have been there, I have to see Rome too.”
19.22: And having sent into Makedonia two of those assisting him, Timotiyos and Ĕrastos, he himself remained in Asia for a time.
19.23: And about that time there came to be a great commotion about the Way.
19.24: For a certain man named Dĕmĕtrios, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, provided no little business to the craftsmen,
19.25: who, having called them together, with the workers of the same, said, “Men, you know that our wealth is from this business.
19.26: “And you see and hear that not only at Ephesos, but throughout almost all Asia, this Sha’ul has persuaded and turned away a large number, saying that they are not mighty ones which are made with hands.
19.27: “And not only is this trade of ours in danger of coming to rejection, but also that the temple of the great female mighty one Artemis whom all Asia and the world worship, shall be regarded as worthless and her greatness diminished.”
19.28: And having heard this, they were filled with rage and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.29: And the entire city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one mind into the theatre, having seized Gaios and Aristarḵos, Makedonians, Sha’ul’s fellow travelers.
19.30: And Sha’ul, intending to go in among the mob, the talmidim did not allow him.
19.31: And some of the officials of Asia, being his friends, sent to him begging him not to risk himself into the theatre.
19.32: Then others indeed shouted this and others that, for the assembly was confused, and most of them did not know why they had come together.
19.33: And some of the crowd instructed Alexandros - the Yahuḏim putting him forward. And Alexandros motioned with his hand, and wanted to make his defense to the people.
19.34: But having recognized that he was Yahuḏi, all with one voice cried out for about two hours, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.35: And the city clerk, having calmed the crowd, said, “Men of Ephesos, what man is there who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is the guardian of the temple of the great female mighty one Artemis, and of that which fell down from Zeus?
19.36: “Therefore, if these are undeniable, you need to be calm, and do not act rashly.
19.37: “For you have brought these men here who are neither temple-robbers nor speaking evil of your female mighty one.
19.38: “If truly then Dĕmĕtrios and his fellow craftsmen have a case against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them accuse one another.
19.39: “And if you have any further complaint, it shall be settled in the regular assembly.
19.40: “For we are in danger of being accused of riot concerning today, there being no reason which we could give to account for this disorderly gathering.”
19.41: And having said this, he dismissed the assembly.

2.1: And when the Day of the Festival of Shaḇuoth had come, they were all with one mind in one place.
2.2: And suddenly there came a sound from the shamayim, as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
2.3: And there appeared to them divided tongues, as of fire, and settled on each one of them.
2.4: And they were all filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh and began to speak with other tongues, as the Ruaḥ gave them to speak.
2.5: Now in Yerushalayim there were dwelling Yahuḏim, dedicated men from every nation under the shamayim.
2.6: And when this sound came to be, the crowd came together, and were confused, because everyone heard them speak in his own language.
2.7: And they were all amazed and marveled, saying to each other, “Look, are not all these who speak Galileans?
2.8: “And how do we hear, each one in our own language in which we were born?
2.9: “Parthians and Maḏites and Ĕylamites, and those dwelling in Aram Naharayim, both Yahuḏah and Kappadokia, Pontus and Asia,
2.10: both Phrugia and Pamphulia, Mitsrayim and the parts of Libuĕ around Kurĕnĕ, visitors from Rome, both Yahuḏim and converts,
2.11: “Krĕtĕans and Araḇs, we hear them speaking in our own tongues the great deeds of Elohim.”
2.12: And they were all amazed, and were puzzled, saying to each other, “What does this mean?”
2.13: And others mocking said, “They have been filled with sweet wine.”
2.14: But Kĕpha, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice and said to them, “Men of Yahuḏah and all those dwelling in Yerushalayim, let this be known to you, and listen closely to my words.
2.15: “For these men are not drunk, as you imagine, since it is only the third hour of the day.
2.16: “But this is what was spoken by the naḇi Yo’ĕl:
2.17: ‘And it shall be in the last days, says Elohim, that I shall pour out of My Ruaḥ on all flesh. And your sons and your daughters shall naḇa, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams,
2.18: and also on My male servants and on My female servants I shall pour out My Ruaḥ in those days, and they shall naḇa.
2.19: ‘And I shall show wonders in the shamayim above and signs in the earth beneath: blood and fire and vapor of smoke.
2.20: ‘The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the coming of the great and splendid day of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.21: ‘And it shall be that everyone who calls on the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be saved.’
2.22: “Men of Yisra’ĕl, hear these words: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth, a Man from Elohim, having been pointed out to you by mighty works, and wonders, and signs which Elohim did through Him in your midst, as you yourselves also know,
2.23: this One, given up by the marked purpose and foreknowledge of Elohim, you have impaled and put to death through the hands of lawless men -
2.24: “Him Elohim raised up, having loosed the pangs of death, because it was impossible that He could be held in its grip.
2.25: “For Dawiḏ says concerning Him, ‘I foresaw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 before me continually, because He is at my right hand, in order that I should not be shaken.
2.26: ‘For this reason my heart rejoiced, and my tongue was glad, and now my flesh shall also rest in expectation,
2.27: because You shall not leave my being in the grave, nor shall You give Your Kind One to see corruption.
2.28: ‘You have made known to me the Ways of ḥai, You shall fill me with joy in Your presence.’
2.29: “Men and brothers, let me speak boldly to you of the ancestor Dawiḏ, that he died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
2.30: “Being a naḇi, then, and knowing that Elohim had sworn with an oath to him: of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, to raise up ha’Mashiaḥ to sit on his throne,
2.31: foreseeing this he spoke concerning the resurrection of ha’Mashiaḥ, that His being was neither left in the grave, nor did His flesh see corruption.
2.32: “Elohim has raised up this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, of which we are all witnesses.
2.33: “Therefore, having been exalted to the right hand of Elohim, and having received from the Father the promise of the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, He poured out this which you now see and hear.
2.34: “For Dawiḏ did not ascend into the shamayim, but he himself said, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Aḏoni, “Sit at My right hand,
2.35: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” ’
2.36: “Therefore let all the house of Yisra’ĕl know for certain that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has made this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, whom you impaled, both Aḏon and Mashiaḥ.”
2.37: And having heard this, they were pierced to the heart, and said to Kĕpha and the rest of the emissaries, “Men, brothers, what shall we do?”
2.38: And Kĕpha said to them, “Repent, and let each one of you be immersed in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ for the forgiveness of sins. And you shall receive the gift of the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.
2.39: “For the promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are far off, as many as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim shall call.”
2.40: And with many other words he earnestly witnessed and urged them, saying, “Be saved from this crooked generation.”
2.41: Then those, indeed, who gladly received his word, were immersed. And on that day about three thousand beings were added to them.
2.42: And they were continuing steadfastly in the teaching of the emissaries, and in the fellowship, and in the breaking of bread, and in the prayers.
2.43: And fear came upon every being, and many wonders and signs were being done through the emissaries.
2.44: And all those who believed were together, and had all in common,
2.45: and sold their possessions and property, and divided them among all, as anyone might have need.
2.46: And day by day, continuing with one mind in the Miqdash, and breaking bread from house to house, they ate their food with gladness and simplicity of heart,
2.47: praising Elohim and having favor with all the people. And the Aḏon added to the assembly those who were being saved, day by day.

20.1: After the uproar had ceased, Sha’ul called the talmidim to him, and having embraced them, went away to go to Makedonia.
20.2: And having gone through those parts, and having encouraged them with many words, he came to Yawan,
20.3: where he spent three months. When he was about to sail to Suria, he decided to return through Makedonia, as a plot was made against him by the Yahuḏim.
20.4: And he was accompanied by Sopatros of Beroia, and Aristarḵos and Sekundos of the Tas’loniqim, and Gaios of Derbĕ, and Timotiyos, and Tuḵikos and Trophimos of Asia.
20.5: And these, going ahead, waited for us at Troas.
20.6: And we sailed away from Philippi after the Days of Matstsoth, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.
20.7: And on one of the shabbathoth, the talmidim having gathered together to break bread, Sha’ul, intending to depart the next day, was reasoning with them and was extending the Word till midnight.
20.8: And there were many lamps in the upper room where they were assembled.
20.9: And a certain young man, by name Eutuḵos, was sitting in a window, being overpowered by a deep sleep. As Sha’ul kept on reasoning, he was overcome by sleep and fell down from the third story, and was picked up dead.
20.10: And Sha’ul, having gone down, fell on him, and embracing him said, “Do not be upset, for his life is in him.”
20.11: Then going up again, and having broken bread and eaten, he talked a long while, even till daybreak, and so went forth.
20.12: And they brought the young man in alive, and were encouraged, not a little.
20.13: And we, going ahead to the ship, sailed to Assos, intending to take Sha’ul on board there, for so he had arranged, intending himself to go on foot.
20.14: And when he met us at Assos, we took him on board and came to Mitulĕnĕ.
20.15: And from there we sailed, and the next day came opposite Ḵios. And the next day we arrived at Samos and remained at Trogullion. And the following day we came to Milĕtos.
20.16: For Sha’ul had decided to sail past Ephesos, so that he might lose no time in Asia, for he was hurrying to be at Yerushalayim, if possible, on the Day of the Festival of Shaḇuoth.
20.17: And from Milĕtos he sent to Ephesos and called for the elders of the assembly.
20.18: And when they had come to him, he said to them, “You know, from the first day that I came to Asia, how I was with you all the time,
20.19: serving the Aḏon with all humility, with many tears and trials which befell me by the plotting of the Yahuḏim,
20.20: as I kept back none that was profitable, but proclaimed it to you, and taught you publicly and from house to house,
20.21: witnessing to Yahuḏim, and also to Yawanites: repentance toward Elohim and belief in our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ
20.22: “And now see, I go bound in the spirit to Yerushalayim, not knowing what is going to meet me there,
20.23: except that the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh witnesses in every city, saying that chains and pressures await me.
20.24: “But I do not count my life of any value to me, so that I might accomplish my mission with joy, and the service which I received from the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, to bear witness to the Good News of the favor of Elohim.
20.25: “And now see, I know that you all, among whom I went about proclaiming the Malḵuth of Elohim, shall see my face no more.
20.26: “Therefore I witness to you this day that I am clear from the blood of all.
20.27: “For I did not keep back from declaring to you all the counsel of Elohim.
20.28: “Therefore take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of Elohim which He has purchased with His own blood.
20.29: “For I know this, that after my departure savage wolves shall come in among you, not sparing the flock.
20.30: “Also from among yourselves men shall arise, speaking distortions, to draw away the talmidim after themselves.
20.31: “Therefore watch, remembering that for three years, night and day, I did not cease to warn each one with tears.
20.32: “And now, brothers, I commit you to Elohim and to the Word of His favor, which is able to build you up and give you an inheritance among all those having been set apart.
20.33: “I have coveted no one’s silver or gold or garments.
20.34: “And you yourselves know that these hands supplied my needs, and for those who were with me.
20.35: “All this I showed you, by laboring like this, that you ought to help the weak. And remember the words of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, that He said, ‘It is happier to give than to receive.’ ”
20.36: And having said this, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
20.37: And there was much weeping among them all, and falling on Sha’ul’s neck, they kissed him,
20.38: distressed most of all because of the word which he had said, that they would see his face no more. And they went with him to the ship.

21.1: And it came to be, when we had torn ourselves away from them, and had launched, we ran a straight course and came to Kos, and the next day to Rhodos, and from there to Patara.
21.2: And having found a ship passing over to Phoinikĕ, we went aboard and launched.
21.3: And having sighted Kupros, and having passed it on the left, we sailed to Suria, and landed at Tsor, for the ship was to unload her cargo there.
21.4: And having found talmidim, we remained there seven days. And they told Sha’ul through the Ruaḥ not to go up to Yerushalayim.
21.5: And when it came to be that our days there were ended, we left and went on, all of them accompanying us, with wives and children, till we were out of the city. And kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
21.6: And having embraced one another, we boarded the ship, and they returned to their homes.
21.7: And when we had completed our voyage from Tsor, we came to Ptolemais. And having greeted the brothers we stayed with them one day.
21.8: And on the next day we left and came to Kaisereia, and went into the house of Philippos the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.
21.9: Now this one had four maiden daughters who naḇu.
21.10: And as we were staying many days, a certain naḇi named Ḥaḡaḇ came down from Yahuḏah,
21.11: and having come to us, he took the girdle of Sha’ul, bound his own hands and feet, and said, “Thus says the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, ‘Thus shall the Yahuḏim at Yerushalayim bind the man who owns this girdle, and deliver him into the hands of the gentiles.’ ”
21.12: And when we heard this, both we and those from that place begged him not to go up to Yerushalayim.
21.13: And Sha’ul answered, “What do you mean by weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Yerushalayim for the Name of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.”
21.14: And as he could not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “Let the desire of the Aḏon be done.”
21.15: And after those days, having made ready, we went up to Yerushalayim.
21.16: And also some of the talmidim from Kaisereia went with us and brought with them one, Mnason of Kupros, an early talmid, with whom we were to lodge.
21.17: And when we had arrived in Yerushalayim, the brothers received us gladly.
21.18: And on the following day Sha’ul went in with us to Ya’aqoḇ, and all the elders came.
21.19: And having greeted them, he was relating one by one what Elohim had done among the gentiles through his service.
21.20: And when they heard it, they praised the Aḏon. And they said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Yahuḏim there are who have believed, and all are ardent for the Torah.
21.21: “And they have been informed about you that you teach all the Yahuḏim who are among the gentiles to forsake Mosheh, saying not to circumcise the children nor to walk according to the practices.
21.22: “What then is it? They shall certainly hear that you have come.
21.23: “So do this, what we say to you: We have four men who have taken a vow.
21.24: “Take them and be cleansed with them, and pay their expenses so that they shave their heads. And all shall know that what they have been informed about you is not so, but that you yourself also walk orderly, keeping the Torah.
21.25: “But concerning the gentiles who believe, we have written and decided that they should keep themselves from what is offered to idols, and blood, and what is strangled, and whoring.”
21.26: Then Sha’ul took the men on the next day, and having been cleansed with them, went into the Miqdash to announce the completion of the days of cleansing - until the offering should be presented for each one of them.
21.27: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Yahuḏim from Asia, seeing him in the Miqdash, were stirring up all the crowd, and they laid hands on him,
21.28: crying out, “Men of Yisra’ĕl, help! This is the man who is teaching all men everywhere against the people, and the Torah, and this place. And besides, he also brought Yawanites into the Miqdash and has profaned this Miqdash.”
21.29: Because they had previously seen Trophimos the Ephesian with him in the city, whom they thought that Sha’ul had brought into the Miqdash.
21.30: And the entire city was moved, and the people rushed together, seized Sha’ul, and dragged him out of the Miqdash. And immediately the doors were shut.
21.31: And while they were seeking to kill him, a report came to the commander of the cohort that all Yerushalayim was in confusion.
21.32: At once he took soldiers and captains, and ran down to them. And they, having seen the commander and the soldiers, stopped beating Sha’ul.
21.33: Then the commander came near and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains, and was asking who he was and what he had done.
21.34: And in the crowd some were shouting this and others that. And not being able to ascertain the truth because of the uproar, he commanded him to be taken into the barracks.
21.35: And when he came to the stairs, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd.
21.36: For a large number of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”
21.37: And as Sha’ul was about to be led into the barracks, he said to the commander, “Am I allowed to say somewhat to you?” And he said, “Do you know Yawanite?
21.38: “Are you not the Mitsrite who some time ago stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand assassins out into the wilderness?”
21.39: But Sha’ul replied, “I am a Yahuḏi from Tarsos, in Kilikia, a citizen of no mean city. And I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”
21.40: And having given him permission, Sha’ul, standing on the stairs motioned with his hand to the people. And when there was a great silence, he spoke in the Iḇri language, saying,

22.1: “Men, brothers, and fathers, hear my defense before you now.”
22.2: And when they heard that he spoke to them in the Iḇri language, they kept greater silence. And he said:
22.3: “I am indeed Yahuḏi, having been born in Tarsos of Kilikia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamli’ĕl, having been instructed according to the exactness of the Torah of our fathers, being ardent for Elohim, as you all are today,
22.4: who persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering up into prisons both men and women,
22.5: as also the kohĕn ha’gadol bears me witness, and all the eldership, from whom I also received letters to the brothers, and went to Dammeseq to bring in chains even those who were there to Yerushalayim to be punished.
22.6: “And it came to be, as I was journeying and coming near Dammeseq, about noon, suddenly a great light shone around me out of the shamayim,
22.7: and I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Sha’ul, Sha’ul, why do you persecute Me?’
22.8: “And I answered, ‘Who are You, Aḏonai?’ And He said to me, ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth, whom you persecute.’
22.9: “And those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they did not hear His voice speaking to me.
22.10: “And I said, ‘What shall I do, Aḏonai?’ And the Aḏon said to me, ‘Rise up, go into Dammeseq, and there you shall be told all that you have been appointed to do.’
22.11: “And as I could not see because of the esteem of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Dammeseq.
22.12: “And a certain Ḥananyah, a dedicated man according to the Torah, being well spoken of by all the Yahuḏim dwelling there,
22.13: came to me, and stood by and said to me, ‘Brother Sha’ul, look up.’ And at that same hour I looked up at him.
22.14: “And he said, ‘The Elohim of our fathers has appointed you to know His desire, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear the voice from His mouth.
22.15: ‘Because you shall be His witness to all men of what you have seen and heard.
22.16: ‘And now, why do you delay? Rise up, be immersed, and wash away your sins, calling on the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’
22.17: “And it came to be, when I returned to Yerushalayim, and while I was praying in the Miqdash, I came to be in a trance,
22.18: and I saw Him saying to me, ‘Hurry and get out of Yerushalayim, speedily, because they shall not accept your witness concerning Me.’
22.19: “And I said, ‘Aḏonai, they know that in every congregation I was imprisoning and beating those who believe on You.
22.20: ‘And when the blood of Your witness Stephanos was shed, I also was standing by giving my approval to his death, and keeping the garments of those who were killing him.’
22.21: “And He said to me, ‘Go, because I shall send you far from here to the gentiles.’ ”
22.22: And they were listening to him until this word, and then they lifted up their voice, saying, “Away with such a one from the earth, for it is not fit that he should live!”
22.23: As they were shouting and throwing off their garments, and throwing dust into the air,
22.24: the commander ordered him to be brought into the barracks, and said that he should be examined by flogging, in order to find out why they were shouting so against him.
22.25: And as they were stretching him out with straps, Sha’ul said to the captain who was standing by, “Is it permitted for you to whip a man who is a Roman, and uncondemned?”
22.26: And when the captain heard, he went and reported to the commander, saying, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman.”
22.27: And having come, the commander said to him, “Say to me, are you a Roman?” And he said, “Yes.”
22.28: And the commander answered, “With a large sum I obtained this citizenship.” And Sha’ul said, “But I was even born so.”
22.29: Then at once those who were about to examine him withdrew from him. And the commander was also afraid after he found out that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
22.30: And on the next day, intending to know for certain why he was accused by the Yahuḏim, he released him, and commanded the chief kohenim and all their council to come, and brought Sha’ul down and put him before them.

23.1: And Sha’ul, looking intently at the council, said, “Men, brothers, I have lived in all good conscience before Elohim until this day.”
23.2: And the kohĕn ha’gadol Ḥananyah commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
23.3: Then Sha’ul said to him, “Elohim is going to strike you, whitewashed wall! And do you sit judging me according to the Torah, and do you command me to be struck contrary to the Torah?”
23.4: And those who stood by said, “Do you revile the kohĕn ha’gadol of Elohim?”
23.5: And Sha’ul said, “I did not know, brothers, that he was the kohĕn ha’gadol, for it has been written, ‘You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people.’ ”
23.6: Now Sha’ul, perceiving that one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, cried out in the council, “Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee, I am being judged concerning the expectation and resurrection of the dead!”
23.7: And when he had said this, there came a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees. And the crowd was divided.
23.8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor messenger nor spirit, but the Pharisees confess both.
23.9: And there was a great uproar. And certain of the scribes of the party of Pharisees rose up and were earnestly contending, saying, “We find no evil in this man. And if a spirit or a messenger has spoken to him, let us not fight against Elohim.”
23.10: And a great dissension having come, the commander, fearing lest Sha’ul would be pulled to pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and seize him from their midst, and bring him into the barracks.
23.11: And on the following night the Aḏon stood by him and said, “Take courage, Sha’ul, for as you have witnessed for Me in Yerushalayim, so you have to bear witness at Rome too.”
23.12: And when it became day, some of the Yahuḏim made a conspiracy and bound themselves under an oath, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Sha’ul.
23.13: And those making this conspiracy were more than forty,
23.14: who, having come to the chief kohenim and elders, said, “We have bound ourselves under a great oath not to eat at all until we have killed Sha’ul.
23.15: “Now, then, you, with the council, inform the commander to have him brought down to you tomorrow, as intending to examine more exactly all about him. And we are ready to kill him before he comes near.”
23.16: And when Sha’ul’s sister’s son heard of their ambush, he went and entered into the barracks and reported to Sha’ul.
23.17: And Sha’ul, having called one of the captains to him, said, “Take this young man to the commander, for he has somewhat to report to him.”
23.18: He indeed then took him and led him to the commander and said, “The prisoner Sha’ul called me to him and asked me to bring this young man to you, having somewhat to say to you.”
23.19: And the commander, having taken him by the hand, went aside by themselves and asked, “What is it that you have to report to me?”
23.20: And he said, “The Yahuḏim have agreed to ask that you bring Sha’ul down to the council tomorrow, as intending to inquire more exactly about him.
23.21: “Therefore, do not let them persuade you, for more than forty of them lie in wait for him, men who have bound themselves by an oath neither to eat nor to drink until they have killed him. And now they are ready, waiting for the promise from you.”
23.22: Then the commander dismissed the young man, having commanded him, “Inform no one that you reported this to me.”
23.23: And having called near a certain two captains, he said, “Get two hundred soldiers ready to go to Kaisereia, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, after the third hour of the night,
23.24: and provide beasts, on which to place Sha’ul, and bring him safely to Phĕlix the governor,”
23.25: having written a letter in this form:
23.26: Klaudius Lusias, to the most excellent governor Phĕlix: Greetings.
23.27: This man, having been seized by the Yahuḏim, and being about to be killed by them, I rescued, having come with soldiers, having learned that he was a Roman.
23.28: And, desiring to know the reason they accused him, I brought him before their council.
23.29: I found out that he was accused concerning questions of their Torah, but there was no charge against him deserving death or chains.
23.30: And when I was informed that there was to be a plot against the man by the Yahuḏim, I sent him immediately to you, having also commanded his accusers to state before you the charges against him. Be strong!
23.31: So the soldiers, as they were commanded, took Sha’ul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
23.32: And on the next day they left the horsemen to go on with him, and returned to the barracks,
23.33: who, having come to Kaisereia, and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Sha’ul to him.
23.34: And the governor, having read it, and having asked of what province he was, and being informed that he was from Kilikia,
23.35: said, “I shall hear you when your accusers arrive also.” And he commanded him to be kept in Hĕrodĕs’ palace.

24.1: And after five days the kohĕn ha’gadol Ḥananyah came down, with the elders, and a certain speaker - Tertullus. And they brought charges against Sha’ul before the governor.
24.2: And when he was called upon, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Having obtained great peace through you, and reforms being brought to this nation by your forethought,
24.3: we accept it always and in all places, most excellent Phĕlix, with all thanks.
24.4: “But in order not to hinder you any further, I beg you to hear us briefly in your gentleness.
24.5: “For having found this man a plague, who stirs up dissension among all the Yahuḏim throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Natsarenes,
24.6: who also tried to profane the Miqdash, and whom we seized, and wanted to judge him according to our law,
24.7: but the commander Lusias came along and with much violence took him out of our hands,
24.8: commanding his accusers to come to you. And by examining him yourself you shall be able to know all these of which we accuse him.”
24.9: And the Yahuḏim also agreed, maintaining that these were so.
24.10: And when the governor had motioned him to speak, Sha’ul answered, “Knowing that for many years you have been a judge of this nation, I gladly defend myself,
24.11: seeing you are able to know that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to Yerushalayim to worship.
