24.12: “And they neither found me in the Miqdash disputing with anyone nor stirring up the crowd, either in the congregations or in the city.
24.13: “Nor are they able to prove the charges of which they now accuse me.
24.14: “And this I confess to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, so I worship the Elohim of my fathers, believing all that has been written in the Torah and in the Neḇi’im,
24.15: having an expectation in Elohim, which they themselves also wait for, that there is to be a resurrection of the dead, both of the righteous and the unrighteous.
24.16: “And in this I exercise myself to have a clear conscience toward Elohim and men always.
24.17: “And after many years I came to bring kind deeds to my nation and offerings,
24.18: at which time certain Yahuḏim from Asia found me cleansed in the Miqdash, neither with a crowd nor with disturbance,
24.19: who ought to be present before you to bring charges if they have any against me.
24.20: “Or else let these themselves say if they found any wrongdoing in me while I stood before the council,
24.21: other than for this one declaration which I cried out, standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged by you today.’ ”
24.22: And having heard this, having known more exactly about the Way, Phĕlix put them off, saying, “When Lusias the commander comes down, I shall decide your case.”
24.23: And he ordered the captain to keep Sha’ul and to have ease, and not to forbid any of his friends to attend to him.
24.24: And after some days, when Phĕlix came with his wife Drousilla, who was a female Yahuḏi, he sent for Sha’ul and heard him concerning the belief in Mashiaḥ.
24.25: And as he reasoned about righteousness, and self-control, and the judgment to come, Phĕlix became frightened and said, “For the present, go. And when I find time I shall send for you.”
24.26: At the same time too he was anticipating that money would be given him by Sha’ul, that he might release him. Therefore he sent for him more often and conversed with him.
24.27: But after two years had passed Porkios Phĕstos succeeded Phĕlix. And wanting to do the Yahuḏim a favor, Phĕlix left Sha’ul bound.

25.1: Phĕstos therefore, having come to the province, three days later went up from Kaisereia to Yerushalayim.
25.2: And the kohĕn ha’gadol and the chief men of the Yahuḏim informed him against Sha’ul, and they begged him,
25.3: asking a favor against him, that he would send him to Yerushalayim - making a plot along the way to kill him.
25.4: Then, indeed, Phĕstos answered that Sha’ul should be kept at Kaisereia, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.
25.5: “Therefore,” he said, “let those who have authority among you go down with me and, if there is any fault in him, accuse this man.”
25.6: And having spent more than ten days among them, he went down to Kaisereia. And on the next day, sitting on the judgment seat, he commanded Sha’ul to be brought.
25.7: And when he had come, the Yahuḏim who had come down from Yerushalayim stood about, bringing many and heavy charges against Sha’ul, which they were unable to prove,
25.8: while Sha’ul said in his own defense, “Neither against the Torah of the Yahuḏim, nor against the Miqdash, nor against Kaisar did I commit any sin.”
25.9: But Phĕstos, wanting to do the Yahuḏim a favor, answering Sha’ul, said, “Do you want to go up to Yerushalayim and be judged before me there concerning these?”
25.10: And Sha’ul said, “I am standing at Kaisar’s judgement seat, where I should be judged. To the Yahuḏim I have done no wrong, as you know well enough.
25.11: “For if indeed I do wrong, or have committed whatever deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is naught in these of which these men accuse me, no one is able to give me up to them. I appeal to Kaisar.”
25.12: Then Phĕstos, having talked with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Kaisar? To Kaisar you shall go!”
25.13: And certain days having passed, Meleḵ Agrippas and Bernikĕ came to Kaisereia to greet Phĕstos.
25.14: And when they had spent many days there, Phĕstos laid Sha’ul’s case before the meleḵ, saying, “There is a man here whom Phĕlix left as a prisoner,
25.15: about whom the chief kohenim and the elders of the Yahuḏim informed me, when I was in Yerushalayim, asking for a judgment against him.
25.16: “To them I answered, ‘It is not the Roman practice to give up any man to destruction before the accused meets the accusers face to face, and has a chance to answer for himself concerning the charge against him.’
25.17: “They, therefore, having come together here, without any delay, I sat on the judgment seat the next day and commanded the man to be brought in.
25.18: “When the accusers stood up, they brought no charge against him such as I expected,
25.19: but had some questions against him about their own worship and about a certain 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, who had died, whom Sha’ul was claiming to be alive.
25.20: “And being uncertain how to investigate these matters, I asked whether he wanted to go to Yerushalayim and there be judged concerning these matters.
25.21: “But when Sha’ul appealed to be kept for the decision of Augustus, I ordered him to be kept until I send him to Kaisar.”
25.22: And Agrippas said to Phĕstos, “I was wanting also to hear the man myself.” And he said, “Tomorrow, you shall hear him.”
25.23: Therefore, on the next day, Agrippas and Bernikĕ having come with great show, and having entered the place of hearing with the commanders and the eminent men of the city, Sha’ul was brought in at the order of Phĕstos.
25.24: And Phĕstos said, “Meleḵ Agrippas and all the men present here with us, you see this one about whom all the community of the Yahuḏim pleaded with me, both at Yerushalayim and here, shouting that he ought not to be living any longer.
25.25: “But I, having found that he had committed naught deserving death, and that he himself had appealed to Augustus, I decided to send him.
25.26: “I have none definite to write to my master concerning him. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and most of all before you, Meleḵ Agrippas, so that after the examination has taken place I might have somewhat to write.
25.27: “For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner and not to signify the charges against him.”

26.1: And Agrippas said to Sha’ul, “You are allowed to speak for yourself.” Then Sha’ul stretched out his hand and made his defense:
26.2: “I think myself fortunate, Meleḵ Agrippas, because today I shall make my defense before you concerning all of which I am accused by the Yahuḏim,
26.3: you being most of all an expert, knowing of all practices and questions which have to do with the Yahuḏim. So, please hear me patiently.
26.4: “Truly, then, all the Yahuḏim know my way of life from youth, which I led from the beginning among my own nation at Yerushalayim,
26.5: since they have known me from the first, if they want to witness, that I lived as a Pharisee according to the strictest sect of our observance.
26.6: “And now I stand and am judged for the expectation of the promise made by Elohim to our fathers,
26.7: to which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving Elohim night and day, expect to attain. Concerning this expectation, O Meleḵ Agrippas, I am accused by the Yahuḏim.
26.8: “Why is it considered ‘unbelievable’ among you if Elohim raises the dead?
26.9: “Therefore, indeed, I thought within myself that I ought to do much against the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth,
26.10: which also I did in Yerushalayim, and I shut up many of the qodeshim in prison, having received authority from the chief kohenim. And when they were put to death, I gave my vote against them.
26.11: “And punishing them often in all the congregations, I compelled them to blaspheme. And being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
26.12: “While thus engaged, as I was journeying to Dammeseq with authority and commission from the chief kohenim,
26.13: at midday, O meleḵ, I saw on the way a light from the shamayim, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who journeyed with me.
26.14: “And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me, and saying in the Iḇri language, ‘Sha’ul, Sha’ul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the prods.’
26.15: “And I said, ‘Who are You, Aḏonai?’ And He said, ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, whom you persecute.
26.16: ‘But rise up, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to appoint you a servant and a witness both of what you saw and of those which I shall reveal to you,
26.17: delivering you from the people, and the gentiles, to whom I now send you,
26.18: to open their eyes, to turn them from darkness to light, and the authority of Satan to Elohim, in order for them to receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are qadosh by belief in Me.’
26.19: “Therefore, Meleḵ Agrippas, I was not disobedient to the vision of the shamayim,
26.20: but declared first to those in Dammeseq and in Yerushalayim, and in all the country of Yahuḏah, and to the gentiles, that they should repent, and turn to Elohim, and do works worthy of repentance.
26.21: “That is why the Yahuḏim seized me in the Miqdash and tried to kill me.
26.22: “Therefore, having obtained help from Elohim, to this day I stand, witnessing both to small and great, saying nil else than what the Neḇi’im and Mosheh said would come -
26.23: that ha’Mashiaḥ would suffer, would be the first to rise from the dead, He would proclaim light to the people and to the gentiles.”
26.24: And while saying this in his defense, Phĕstos said with a loud voice, “Sha’ul, you are mad! Much learning is turning you to madness!”
26.25: But Sha’ul said, “I am not mad, most excellent Phĕstos, but I speak words of truth and sense.
26.26: “For the meleḵ, before whom I also speak boldly, knows this. For l am persuaded that none of these are hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.
26.27: “Meleḵ Agrippas, do you believe the Neḇi’im? I know that you do believe.”
26.28: And Agrippas said to Sha’ul, “With a little you might persuade me to become a Mashiaḥi!”
26.29: And Sha’ul said, “Much or little, I pray to Elohim that not only you, but also all who hear me today, might become such as I also am, except for these chains.”
26.30: And when he had said this, the meleḵ stood up, as well as the governor and Bernikĕ and those sitting with them,
26.31: and having withdrawn, they spoke to each other, saying, “This man is doing naught deserving death or chains.”
26.32: And Agrippas said to Phĕstos, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Kaisar.”

27.1: And when it was decided that we should sail to Italia, they delivered Sha’ul and some other prisoners to one named Yulios, captain of the Augustan regiment.
27.2: And having embarked in a ship from Adramyttium, about to sail along the coasts of Asia, we launched. Aristarḵos, a Makedonian of Thessalonikĕ, was with us.
27.3: And on the next day we landed at Tsiḏon. And Yulios treated Sha’ul kindly and allowed him to go to his friends to receive attention.
27.4: And from there we put out to sea and sailed close to Kupros, because the winds were against us.
27.5: And having sailed over the sea along Kilikia and Pamphulia, we came to Mura, of Lukia.
27.6: And there the captain, having found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italia, put us on board.
27.7: And having sailed slowly many days, and arriving with difficulty off Knidos, the wind not allowing us to proceed, we sailed close to Krĕtĕ, off Salmonĕ.
27.8: And passing it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasaia.
27.9: And much time having passed, and the sailing now being dangerous, because the Fast was already over, Sha’ul advised them,
27.10: saying, “Men, I see that this voyage is going to end with damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and ship, but also our lives.”
27.11: But the captain was persuaded by the pilot and the owner of the ship, rather than what Sha’ul said.
27.12: And because the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the greater part advised to launch from there too, if somehow they were able to reach Phoinikĕ, a harbor of Krĕtĕ facing southwest and northwest, to pass the winter.
27.13: And a south wind blowing softly, thinking they had obtained their purpose, having lifted anchor, they sailed close along Krĕtĕ.
27.14: And not long after, a stormy wind rushed down from it, called Northeaster.
27.15: And when the ship was caught, and unable to head against the wind, we let her go and were driven.
27.16: And having run under a small island called Klaudĕ, we were hardly able to control the small boat.
27.17: And having hoisted it, they used helps to undergird the ship. And fearing lest they should run aground on Surtis, they lowered the tackle and so were driven.
27.18: And because we were exceedingly storm-tossed, the next day they began to throw overboard.
27.19: And on the third day we threw out the ship’s tackle with our own hands.
27.20: When, now, neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small storm beat on us, all expectancy that we would be saved was taken away.
27.21: And when there had been a long abstinence from food, then Sha’ul, standing in the midst of them, said, “Truly, men, you should have listened to me not to have sailed from Krĕtĕ and sustained this damage and loss.
27.22: “And now I urge you to take courage, for there shall be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
27.23: “For tonight a messenger of the Elohim to whom I belong and whom I serve, stood by me,
27.24: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Sha’ul, you have to be brought before Kaisar. And look, Elohim has favorably given you all those who sail with you.’
27.25: “Therefore take courage, men, for I believe Elohim that it shall be according to the way it was spoken to me.
27.26: “However, we need to run aground on some island.”
27.27: And when the fourteenth night came, as we were driven up and down in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors suspected that they were drawing near some land.
27.28: So, taking soundings, they found it to be twenty fathoms. And a little farther on they took soundings again and found it to be fifteen fathoms.
27.29: And, fearing lest we should run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern, and were praying for day to come.
27.30: But when the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under pretense of going to cast out anchors from the prow,
27.31: Sha’ul said to the captain and the soldiers, “If these do not remain in the ship, it is impossible for you to be saved.”
27.32: Then the soldiers cut the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.
27.33: And when day was about to come, Sha’ul urged them all to take food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day you have continued waiting without food, and eaten naught.
27.34: “So I urge you to take food, for this concerns your safety, since not a hair shall fall from the head of any of you.”
27.35: And having said this, he took bread and gave thanks to Elohim in the presence of them all. And when he had broken it he began to eat.
27.36: And they were all encouraged, and also took food themselves.
27.37: And all of us were two hundred and seventy-six beings in the ship.
27.38: And being satisfied with food, they were lightening the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
27.39: And when day came, they did not recognize the land, but they noted a certain bay with a beach, onto which they planned to run the ship if possible.
27.40: And having cast off the anchors, they left them in the sea, meanwhile untying the rudder ropes. And they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
27.41: But coming upon a place where two seas met, they grounded the ship, and the prow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was broken by the pounding of the surf.
27.42: And the soldiers intended to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.
27.43: But the captain, intending to save Sha’ul, kept them from their intention, and commanded those able to swim to jump first and get to land,
27.44: and the rest, some indeed on boards, and some on items of the ship. And so it came to be that all reached the land in safety.

28.1: And having come to safety, they then learned that the island was called Melitĕ.
28.2: And the foreigners showed us extraordinary kindness, for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.
28.3: But Sha’ul, having gathered a bundle of sticks, and having laid them on the fire, an adder came out because of the heat, and fastened itself on his hand.
28.4: And when the foreigners saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to each other, “This man is certainly a murderer, whom, though saved from the sea, still right-ruling does not allow to live.”
28.5: Then, indeed, he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no evil.
28.6: And expecting that he would swell up or suddenly fall down dead, they waited for a long time and saw no harm come to him, changing their minds they said that he was a mighty one.
28.7: And in the neighborhood of that place there were lands of the chief of the island, whose name was Poplius, who received us and housed us in a friendly way for three days.
28.8: And it came to be that the father of Poplius lay sick with fever and dysentery. Sha’ul went in to him, and having prayed he laid his hands on him and healed him.
28.9: And when this took place, the rest of those on the island who had diseases also came and were healed,
28.10: who also respected us in many ways. And when we were departing, they provided for our needs.
28.11: And after three months we launched in an Alexandrian ship which had wintered at the island, and whose figurehead was “Twin Brothers.”
28.12: And having landed at Surakousai, we stayed three days,
28.13: from which place we went round and arrived at Rhegium. And after one day the south wind blew, and the second day we came to Potioloi,
28.14: where we found brothers, and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we went toward Rome.
28.15: And when the brothers there heard about us, they came to meet us as far as Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Sha’ul saw them, he thanked Elohim and took courage.
28.16: And when we came to Rome, the captain delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Sha’ul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.
28.17: And it came to be after three days that Sha’ul called the leaders of the Yahuḏim together. And when they had come together, he said to them, “Men, brothers, though I have done naught against our people or the practices of our fathers, I was delivered as a prisoner from Yerushalayim into the hands of the Romans,
28.18: who, when they had examined me, intended to let me go, because there was no cause for putting me to death.
28.19: “But the Yahuḏim spoke against it, and I was compelled to appeal to Kaisar, not that I had any accusation against my nation.
28.20: “This therefore is the reason I called for you, to see you and speak with you. It is because of the expectation of Yisra’ĕl that I am bound with this chain.”
28.21: And they said to him, “We neither received letters from Yahuḏah concerning you, nor have any of the brothers who came reported or spoken whatever wicked about you.
28.22: “And we think it right to hear from you what you think, for indeed, concerning this sect, we know that it is spoken against everywhere.”
28.23: And having appointed him a day, many came to him where he was staying, to whom he was explaining, earnestly witnessing about the Malḵuth of Elohim, and persuading them concerning 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 from both the Torah of Mosheh and the Neḇi’im, from morning until evening.
28.24: And some indeed were persuaded by what was said, but some believed not.
28.25: And disagreeing with one another, they began to leave, after Sha’ul had spoken one word, “The Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh rightly spoke through Yeshayahu the naḇi to our fathers,
28.26: saying, ‘Go to this people and say, “Hearing you shall hear but by no means understand, and seeing you shall see but by no means perceive,
28.27: for the heart of this people has become thickened, and with their ears they heard heavily, and they have closed their eyes, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back, and I should heal them.” ’
28.28: “Therefore let it be known to you that the deliverance of Elohim has been sent to the gentiles, and they shall hear!”
28.29: And when he had said these words, the Yahuḏim went away and had a great dispute among themselves.
28.30: And Sha’ul stayed two entire years in his own rented house, and was receiving all who came to him,
28.31: proclaiming the Malḵuth of Elohim and teaching about the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ with all boldness, unhindered.

3.1: And Kĕpha and Yoḥanan were going up to the Miqdash at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
3.2: And a certain man, lame from his birth, was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the Miqdash which is called Yaphah, to ask alms from those entering into the Miqdash,
3.3: who, seeing Kĕpha and Yoḥanan about to go into the Miqdash, asked for alms.
3.4: And Kĕpha, with Yoḥanan, looking steadfastly at him, said, “Look at us.”
3.5: And he gave heed to them, expecting to receive whatever from them.
3.6: But Kĕpha said, “I do not have silver and gold, but what I do possess, this I give you: In the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ of Natsareth, rise up and walk.”
3.7: And taking him by the right hand he lifted him up, and immediately his feet and ankle bones were made firm.
3.8: And leaping up, he stood and walked, and went in with them into the Miqdash, walking and leaping and praising Elohim.
3.9: And all the people saw him walking and praising Elohim.
3.10: And they recognized him, that it was he who sat begging alms at the Lovely Gate of the Miqdash. And they were filled with wonder and amazement at what befell him.
3.11: And as the lame man who was healed was clinging to Kĕpha and Yoḥanan, all the people ran together to them in the porch which is called Shelomoh’s, greatly amazed.
3.12: And seeing it, Kĕpha responded to the people, “Men of Yisra’ĕl, why do you marvel at this? Or why look so intently at us, as though by our own power or reverence we have made him walk?
3.13: “The Elohim of Aḇraham, and of Yitsḥaq, and of Ya’aqoḇ, the Elohim of our fathers, esteemed His Servant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, whom you delivered up and denied in the presence of Pilatus, when he had decided to release Him.
3.14: “But you denied the Qodesh and Righteous One, and asked that a man, a murderer, be granted you.
3.15: “But you killed the Leader of ḥai, whom Elohim raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.
3.16: “And by the belief in His Name, this one whom you see and know, His Name made strong, and the belief which comes through Him has given him this perfect healing before all of you.
3.17: “And now, brothers, I know that you did it in ignorance, as your rulers did too.
3.18: “But this is how Elohim has filled what He had announced beforehand through the mouth of all the neḇi’im, that His Mashiaḥ was to suffer.
3.19: “Repent therefore and turn back, for the blotting out of your sins, in order that times of refreshing might come from the presence of the Aḏon,
3.20: and that He sends 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, pre-appointed for you,
3.21: whom the shamayim needs to receive until the times of restoration of all, of which Elohim spoke through the mouth of all His qodesh neḇi’im since of old.
3.22: “For Mosheh truly said to the fathers, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall raise up for you a Naḇi like me from your brothers. Him you shall hear according to all of what He says to you.
3.23: ‘And it shall be that every being who does not hear that Naḇi shall be utterly destroyed from among the people.’
3.24: “And likewise, all the neḇi’im who have spoken, from Shemu’ĕl and those following, have also announced these days.
3.25: “You are sons of the neḇi’im, and of the Covenant which Elohim made with our fathers, saying to Aḇraham, ‘And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be given beraḵah.’
3.26: “To you first, Elohim, having raised up His Servant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, sent Him to baraḵ you, in turning away each one of you from your wicked ways.”

4.1: And as they were speaking to the people, the kohenim and the captain of the Miqdash, and the Sadducees, came upon them,
4.2: being annoyed because they taught the people and announced the resurrection from the dead in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
4.3: And they arrested them, and put them in jail until the next day, for it was already evening.
4.4: But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men became about five thousand.
4.5: And it came to be, on the next day, that their rulers and elders and scribes,
4.6: as well as Ḥanan the kohĕn ha’gadol, and Qayapha, and Yoḥanan, and Alexandros, and as many as were descendants of the kohĕn ha’gadol assembled at Yerushalayim.
4.7: And having placed them in the middle, they asked, “By what power or in what Name did you do this?”
4.8: Then Kĕpha, filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders of Yisra’ĕl:
4.9: “If today we are called to account for a good deed towards a sick man, by whom he has been healed,
4.10: let it be known to all of you, and to all the people of Yisra’ĕl, that in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ of Natsareth, whom you impaled, whom Elohim raised from the dead, by Him this one stands before you, healthy.
4.11: “This is ‘the stone which was rejected by you builders, which has become the chief cornerstone.’
4.12: “And there is no deliverance in anyone else, for there is no other Name under the shamayim given among men by which we need to be saved.”
4.13: And seeing the boldness of Kĕpha and Yoḥanan, and perceiving that they were unlearned and ordinary men, they marveled. And they recognized that they had been with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
4.14: And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they could not contradict it.
4.15: But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they consulted with one another,
4.16: saying, “What shall we do to these men? For, indeed, that an outstanding miracle has been done through them is apparent to all those dwelling in Yerushalayim, and we are unable to deny it.
4.17: “But in order that it spreads no further among the people, let us strongly threaten them, to speak no more to anyone in this Name.”
4.18: And they called them and commanded them not to speak at all nor to teach in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
4.19: But Kĕpha and Yoḥanan answering them, said, ‘Whether it is right in the sight of Elohim to listen to you more than to Elohim, you judge.
4.20: “For it is impossible for us not to speak of what we saw and heard.”
4.21: And having threatened them further, they released them, finding no way of punishing them, because of the people, because they were all praising Elohim for what had been done.
4.22: For the man was over forty years old on whom this miracle of healing had been done.
4.23: And having been released, they went to their own and reported all that the chief kohenim and elders said to them.
4.24: And having heard that, they lifted up their voice to Elohim with one mind and said, “Aḏonai, You are Elohim, who made the shamayim and the earth and the sea, and all that is in them,
4.25: who by the mouth of Your servant Dawiḏ have said, ‘Why did the gentiles rage, and the people plot in vain?
4.26: ‘The melaḵim of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and against His Mashiaḥ.’
4.27: “For truly, in this city there were gathered together against Your qodesh Servant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, whom You anointed, both Hĕrodĕs and Pontius Pilatus, with the gentiles and the people of Yisra’ĕl
4.28: to do whatever Your hand and Your purpose decided before to be done.
4.29: “And now, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, look on their threats, and give to Your servants all boldness to speak Your Word,
4.30: by stretching out Your hand for healing, and signs, and wonders to take place through the Name of Your qodesh Servant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.”
4.31: And when they had prayed, the place where they came together was shaken. And they were all filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, and they spoke the Word of Elohim with boldness.
4.32: And the group of those who believed were of one heart and one being. And no one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, but they had all in common.
4.33: And with great power the emissaries gave witness to the resurrection of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and great favor was upon them all.
4.34: For there was not anyone needy among them, for all who were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of what was sold,
4.35: and laid them at the feet of the emissaries, and they distributed to each as anyone had need.
4.36: And Yosĕph, who was also called Barnaḇah by the emissaries - which translated means, son of encouragement - a Lĕwite, a native of Kupros,
4.37: having land, sold it, and brought the proceeds and laid it at the feet of the emissaries.

5.1: But a certain man named Ḥananyah, with Sappirah his wife, sold a possession.
5.2: And he kept back from the price, his wife also being aware of it, and brought a certain part and laid it at the feet of the emissaries.
5.3: But Kĕpha said, “Ḥananyah, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh and keep back from the price of the land for yourself?
5.4: “While it remained, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not in your authority? Why have you conceived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men but to Elohim.”
5.5: Then Ḥananyah, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came upon all those who heard of this.
5.6: But the young men arose and wrapped him up, carried him out and buried him.
5.7: And it came to be, about three hours later, that his wife came in, not knowing what had taken place.
5.8: And Kĕpha responded to her, “Say to me whether you sold the land for so much?” And she said, “Yes, for so much.”
5.9: So Kĕpha said to her, “Why have you agreed to try the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? Look, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they shall carry you out.”
5.10: And immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. And the young men came in and found her dead, and carrying her out, they buried her beside her husband.
5.11: And great fear came upon all the assembly and upon all who heard of this.
5.12: And through the hands of the emissaries many signs and wonders were done among the people. And they were all with one mind in Shelomoh’s Porch.
5.13: But of the rest no one had the courage to join them, however, the people made much of them.
5.14: And more believers were added to the Aḏon, large numbers of both men and women,
5.15: so that they brought the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, that at least the shadow of Kĕpha, passing by, might fall on some of them.
5.16: A large number also gathered from the surrounding cities to Yerushalayim, bringing sick ones and those who were troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.
5.17: But the kohĕn ha’gadol rose up, and all those with him, which is the sect of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy,
5.18: and seized the emissaries and put them in the public jail.
5.19: But a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 opened the prison doors at night and brought them out, and said,
5.20: “Go and stand in the Miqdash and speak to the people all the Words of this ḥai.”
5.21: Now when they heard, they went into the Miqdash early in the morning, and were teaching. But the kohĕn ha’gadol and those with him came and called the council together, with all the elders of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and sent to the prison for them to be brought.
5.22: But having come, the officers did not find them in the prison, and they went back and reported it,
5.23: saying, “We found the prison shut in all safety, and the watches standing outside before the doors. But having opened them, we found no one inside!”
5.24: And as the kohĕn ha’gadol and the captain of the Miqdash and the chief kohenim heard these words, they were puzzled and wondered what this might be.
5.25: But one came and reported to them, saying, “Look, the men whom you put in prison are standing in the Miqdash and teaching the people!”
5.26: Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, not with force, for they feared the people, lest they should be stoned.
5.27: And having brought them, they put them before the council and the kohĕn ha’gadol asked them,
5.28: saying, “Did we not strictly command you not to teach in this Name? And look, you have filled Yerushalayim with your teaching, and intend to bring the blood of this Man upon us!”
5.29: And Kĕpha and the other emissaries answering, said, “We have to obey Elohim rather than men.
5.30: “The Elohim of our fathers raised up 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 whom you killed by hanging on a timber.
5.31: “Him, a Prince and a Savior, Elohim has exalted to His right hand, to give repentance to Yisra’ĕl and forgiveness of sins.
5.32: “And we are His witnesses to these matters, and so also is the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh whom Elohim has given to those who obey Him.”
5.33: And those hearing were cut through, and took counsel to kill them.
5.34: But a certain one in the council stood up, a Pharisee named Gamli’ĕl, a teacher of the Torah, respected by all the people, and ordered them to put the emissaries outside for a little while,
5.35: and said to them, “Men of Yisra’ĕl, take heed to yourselves what you intend to do to these men.
5.36: “For before these days Toḏah rose up, claiming to be somebody. A number of men, about four hundred, joined him. He was slain, and all who obeyed him were dispersed, and came to naught.
5.37: “After him, Yahuḏah of Galil rose up in the days of the census, and drew away many people after him. He also perished, and all who obeyed him were scattered.
5.38: “And now I say to you, stay away from these men and leave them alone, because if this plan or this work is of men, it shall be overthrown,
5.39: but if it is of Elohim, you are unable to overthrow it, lest you even be found to fight against Elohim.”
5.40: And they heeded his advice, and having called for the emissaries, beating them, they commanded that they should not speak in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and let them go.
5.41: Then indeed they went rejoicing from the presence of the council, because they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His Name.
5.42: And daily in the Miqdash, and in every house, they did not cease teaching and bringing the Good News: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ!

6.1: And in those days, when the talmidim were increasing, there arose a grumbling against the Iḇrim by the Yawanites, because their widows were overlooked in the daily serving.
6.2: So the twelve summoned the group of the talmidim and said, “It is not pleasing for us to leave the Word of Elohim and serve tables.
6.3: “Therefore, brothers, seek out from among you seven men who are known to be filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh and wisdom, whom we shall appoint for this duty,
6.4: but we shall give ourselves continually to prayer and to serving the Word.”
6.5: And the word pleased the entire group. And they chose Stephanos, a man filled with belief and the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, and Philippos, and Proḵoros, and Nikanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nikolaos, a convert from Antioḵeus,
6.6: whom they put before the emissaries. And when they had prayed, they laid hands on them.
6.7: And the Word of Elohim spread, and the number of the talmidim increased greatly in Yerushalayim, and a great many of the kohenim were obedient to the belief.
6.8: And Stephanos, filled with belief and power, did great wonders and signs among the people.
6.9: But some of those of the so-called Congregation of the Freedmen - Kurĕnaions, Alexandrians, and those from Kilikia and Asia - rose up, disputing with Stephanos,
6.10: but they were unable to resist the wisdom and the Ruaḥ by which he spoke.
6.11: Then they instigated men to say, “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Mosheh and Elohim.”
6.12: And they stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, so they came upon him, seized him, and brought him to the council.
6.13: And they presented false witnesses who said, “This man does not cease to speak blasphemous words against this Miqdash and the Torah,
6.14: for we have heard him saying that this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth shall overthrow this place and change the institutes which Mosheh delivered unto us.”
6.15: And all who sat in the council, looking steadily at him, saw his face was like the face of a messenger.

7.1: And the kohĕn ha’gadol said, “Is this so?”
7.2: And he replied, “Men, brothers and fathers, listen: The Elohim of esteem appeared to our father Aḇraham when he was in Aram Naharayim, before he dwelt in Ḥaran,
7.3: and said to him, ‘Come out of your land and from your relatives, and come here, into a land that I shall show you.’
7.4: “Then he came out of the land of the Kasdites and dwelt in Ḥaran. And from there, after the death of his father, He removed him to this land in which you now dwell.
7.5: “And He gave him no inheritance in it, not a foot of it. But He promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him, when as yet he had no child.
7.6: “And Elohim spoke in this way: that his seed would be sojourning in a foreign land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
7.7: ‘And the nation to whom they shall be enslaved, I shall judge,’ said Elohim, ‘and after that they shall come out and serve Me in this place.’
7.8: “And He gave him the covenant of circumcision. And so he brought forth Yitsḥaq and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Yitsḥaq - Ya’aqoḇ, and Ya’aqoḇ - the twelve ancestors.
7.9: “And the ancestors, becoming jealous, sold Yosĕph into Mitsrayim. But Elohim was with him,
7.10: and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, meleḵ of Mitsrayim. And he appointed him governor over Mitsrayim and all his house.
7.11: “Then a scarcity of food and great distress came over all the land of Mitsrayim and Kena’an, and our fathers found no food.
7.12: “But Ya’aqoḇ heard that there was grain in Mitsrayim, and he sent out our fathers the first time,
7.13: and at the second time Yosĕph was made known to his brothers, and Yosĕph’s race became known to the Pharaoh.
7.14: “And Yosĕph sent and called his father Ya’aqoḇ and all his relatives to him, seventy-five people.
7.15: “And Ya’aqoḇ went down to Mitsrayim, and died, he and our fathers,
7.16: and they were brought over to Sheḵem and laid in the tomb that Aḇraham bought for a price of silver from the sons of Ḥamor, of Sheḵem.
7.17: “But as the time of the promise drew near which Elohim had sworn to Aḇraham, the people increased and multiplied in Mitsrayim
7.18: until another meleḵ arose who did not know Yosĕph.
7.19: “Having dealt treacherously with our race, this one mistreated our fathers, making them expose their children, so that they should not live.
7.20: “At that time Mosheh was born, and he was well-pleasing to Elohim. And he was reared three months in the house of his father.
7.21: “But when he was exposed, the daughter of Pharaoh took him up and reared him as her own son.
7.22: “And Mosheh was instructed in all the wisdom of the Mitsrites, and was mighty in words and works.
7.23: “And when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Yisra’ĕl.
7.24: “And seeing one of them being wronged, he defended and revenged him who was oppressed, smiting the Mitsrite.
7.25: “And he thought that his brothers would have understood that Elohim would give deliverance to them by his hand, but they did not understand.
7.26: “And the next day he appeared to two of them as they were fighting, and urged them to peace, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers, why do you wrong one another?’
7.27: “But he who was wronging his neighbor pushed him away, saying, ‘Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?
7.28: ‘Do you want to kill me as you killed the Mitsrite yesterday?’
7.29: “And at this saying, Mosheh fled and became a sojourner in the land of Miḏyan, where he fathered two sons.
7.30: “And after forty years were completed, a Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush, in the wilderness of Mount Sinai.
7.31: “And Mosheh, seeing it, marveled at the sight, and coming near to look, the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to him,
7.32: saying, ‘I am the Elohim of your fathers, the Elohim of Aḇraham and the Elohim of Yitsḥaq and the Elohim of Ya’aqoḇ.’ And Mosheh trembled and did not have the courage to look.
7.33: ‘But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, “Take your sandals off your feet, for the place where you stand is qodesh ground.
7.34: “I have certainly seen the evil treatment of my people who are in Mitsrayim, and I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them. And now come, let Me send you to Mitsrayim.” ’
7.35: “This Mosheh whom they had refused, saying, ‘Who made you a ruler and a judge?’ - this one Elohim sent to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the Messenger who appeared to him in the bush.
7.36: “This one led them out, after he had done wonders and signs in the land of Mitsrayim, and in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness forty years.
7.37: “This is the Mosheh who said to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall raise up for you a Naḇi like me from your brothers. Him you shall hear.’
7.38: “This is he who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the Messenger who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received the living Words to give to us,
7.39: unto whom our fathers would not become obedient, but thrust away, and in their hearts they turned back to Mitsrayim,
7.40: saying to Aharon, ‘Make us mighty ones to go before us, for this Mosheh who led us out of the land of Mitsrayim, we do not know what has become of him.’
7.41: “And they made a calf in those days, and brought an offering to the idol, and were rejoicing in the works of their own hands.
7.42: “So Elohim turned and gave them up to worship the host of the shamayim, as it has been written in the Book of the Neḇi’im, ‘Did you bring slaughtered beasts and offerings unto Me during forty years in the wilderness, O house of Yisra’ĕl?
7.43: ‘And you took up the tent of Moleḵ, and the star of your mighty one Kiyyun, images which you made to bow before them. Therefore I shall remove you beyond Baḇel.’
7.44: “The Tent of Witness was with our fathers in the wilderness, as He appointed, instructing Mosheh to make it according to the pattern that he had seen,
7.45: which our fathers, having received it in turn, also brought with Yahoshua into the land possessed by the gentiles, whom Elohim drove out before the face of our fathers until the days of Dawiḏ,
7.46: who found favor before Elohim and asked to find a dwelling for the Elohim of Ya’aqoḇ,
7.47: but Shelomoh built Him a house.
7.48: “However, the Most High does not dwell in dwellings made with hands, as the naḇi says:
7.49: ‘The shamayim is My throne, and earth is My footstool. What house shall you build for Me? Says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, or what is the place of My rest?
7.50: ‘Has My hand not made all these?’
7.51: “You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, as your fathers did, you also do.
7.52: “Which of the neḇi’im did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who before announced the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you now have become the betrayers and murderers,
7.53: who received the Torah as it was ordained by messengers, but did not watch over it.”
7.54: And hearing this they were cut to the heart and gnashed the teeth at him.
7.55: But he, being filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, looked steadily into the shamayim and saw the esteem of Elohim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 standing at the right hand of Elohim,
7.56: and he said, “Look! I see the shamayim opened and the Bĕn of Aḏam standing at the right hand of Elohim!”
7.57: And crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears, and rushed upon him with one mind,
7.58: and threw him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Sha’ul.
7.59: And they were stoning Stephanos as he was calling and saying, “Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, receive my spirit.”
7.60: And kneeling down he cried out with a loud voice, “Aḏonai, do not hold this sin against them.” And having said this, he fell asleep.

8.1: And Sha’ul was giving approval to his death. And on that day there was a great persecution against the assembly which was at Yerushalayim, and they were all scattered throughout the countries of Yahuḏah and Shomeron, except the emissaries.
8.2: And dedicated men buried Stephanos, and made great lamentation over him.
8.3: But Sha’ul was ravaging the assembly, entering every house, and dragging off men and women, putting them in prison.
8.4: Then those who had been scattered went everywhere bringing the Good News: the Word!
8.5: And going down to the city of Shomeron Philippos proclaimed Mashiaḥ to them.
8.6: And the crowds with one mind heeded what Philippos said, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did.
8.7: For unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed, crying with a loud voice, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
8.8: And there came to be great joy in that city.
8.9: Now there was a certain man called Shim’on, who formerly was practicing magic in the city and astonishing the people of Shomeron, claiming to be someone great,
8.10: to whom they all were giving heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This one is the power of Elohim, which is great.”
8.11: And they were giving heed to him because for a long time he had amazed them with his magic.
8.12: And when they believed Philippos as he brought the Good News about the Malḵuth of Elohim and the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, both men and women were immersed.
8.13: And Shim’on himself also believed. And when he was immersed he continued with Philippos, and was amazed, seeing the miracles and signs which took place.
8.14: And when the emissaries who were at Yerushalayim heard that Shomeron had received the Word of Elohim, they sent Kĕpha and Yoḥanan to them,
8.15: who, when they had come down, prayed for them to receive the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh,
8.16: which had not yet fallen, on any of them, but they had only been immersed in the Name of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
8.17: Then they laid hands on them, and they received the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.
8.18: And Shim’on, seeing that through the laying on of the hands of the emissaries the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh was given, he offered them money,
8.19: saying, “Give me this authority too, so that anyone I lay hands on shall receive the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.”
8.20: But Kĕpha said to him, “Let your silver perish with you, because you thought to buy the gift of Elohim through money!
8.21: “You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not right before Elohim.
8.22: “Repent therefore of this evil of yours, and plead with Elohim, if perhaps the intention of your heart shall be forgiven you.
8.23: “For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and bound by unrighteousness.”
8.24: But Shim’on answering, said, “Plead with the Aḏon for me, so that none of what you had said shall come upon me.”
8.25: Then after they had earnestly witnessed and spoken the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, they returned to Yerushalayim, bringing the Good News in many villages of the Shomeronites.
8.26: But a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Philippos, saying, “Arise and go toward the south along the way which goes down from Yerushalayim to Azzah.” This is desert.
8.27: And he arose and went, and saw, a man of Kush, a eunuch of great authority under Kandakĕ the malkah of the Kushites, who was in charge of all her treasury, and had come to Yerushalayim to worship,
8.28: and was returning. And sitting in his chariot, he was reading the naḇi Yeshayahu.
8.29: And the Ruaḥ said to Philippos, “Go near and join yourself to this chariot.”
8.30: And running up, Philippos heard him reading the naḇi Yeshayahu, and said, “Do you know what you are reading?”
8.31: And he said, “How am I able, unless someone guides me?” And he called Philippos near, to come up and sit with him.
8.32: And the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this, “He was led as a sheep to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so He opened not His mouth.
8.33: “In His humiliation He was deprived of right-ruling. And who shall declare His generation? Because His ḥai is taken from the earth.”
8.34: And the eunuch, answering Philippos, said, “I ask you, about whom does the naḇi say this, about himself or about some other?”
8.35: And Philippos opening his mouth, and beginning at this Scripture, brought to him the Good News: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏!
8.36: And as they were going on the way, they came to some water. And the eunuch said, “Look, water! What hinders me from being immersed?”
8.37: And Philippos said, “If you believe with all your heart, it is permitted.” And he answering, said, “I believe that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ is the Bĕn of Elohim.”
8.38: And he commanded the chariot to stand still. And both Philippos and the eunuch went down into the water, and he immersed him.
8.39: And when they came up out of the water, the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 caught Philippos away, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went his way, rejoicing.
8.40: Philippos, however, was found at Ashdoḏ. And passing through, he brought the Good News in all the cities until he came to Kaisereia.

9.1: But Sha’ul, still breathing threats and murder against the talmidim of the Aḏon, having come to the kohĕn ha’gadol,
9.2: asked from him letters to the congregations of Dammeseq, so that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, to bring them bound to Yerushalayim.
9.3: And it came to be, that as he journeyed, he came near Dammeseq, and suddenly a light flashed around him from the shamayim.
9.4: And he fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to him, “Sha’ul, Sha’ul, why do you persecute Me?”
9.5: And he said, “Who are You, Aḏonai?” And the Aḏon said, “I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, whom you persecute. It is hard for you to kick against the prods.”
9.6: Both trembling, and being astonished, he said, “Aḏonai, what do You want me to do?” And the Aḏon said to him, “Arise and go into the city, and you shall be told what you have to do.”
9.7: And the men journeying with him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice but seeing no one.
9.8: And Sha’ul arose from the ground, but when his eyes were opened he saw no one. And leading him by the hand they brought him into Dammeseq.
9.9: And he was three days without sight, and did not eat nor drink.
9.10: And there was at Dammeseq a certain talmid, by name Ḥananyah. And the Aḏon said unto him in a vision, “Ḥananyah!” And he said, “Here I am, Aḏonai.”
9.11: And the Aḏon said to him, “Arise and go to the street called Straight, and seek in the house of Yahuḏah for one called Sha’ul of Tarsos, for look, he is praying,
9.12: and has seen in a vision a man named Ḥananyah coming in and laying his hand on him, so as to see again.”
9.13: And Ḥananyah answered, “Aḏonai, I have heard from many about this man, how many evils he did to Your qodeshim in Yerushalayim,
9.14: and here he has authority from the chief kohenim to bind all those calling on Your Name.”
9.15: But the Aḏon said to him, “Go, for he is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My Name before nations, melaḵim, and the children of Yisra’ĕl.
9.16: “For I shall show him how much he has to suffer for My Name.”
9.17: And Ḥananyah went away and went into the house. And laying his hands on him he said, “Brother Sha’ul, the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, who appeared to you on the way as you came, has sent me, so that you might see again and be filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.”
9.18: And immediately there fell from his eyes, as it were scales, and he received his sight. And rising up, he was immersed.
9.19: And having received food, he was strengthened. And Sha’ul was with the talmidim at Dammeseq some days.
9.20: And immediately he proclaimed ha’Mashiaḥ in the congregations, that He is the Bĕn of Elohim.
9.21: And all who heard were amazed, and said, “Is this not he who destroyed those calling on this Name in Yerushalayim, and has come here for this, to take them bound to the chief kohenim?”
9.22: But Sha’ul kept increasing in strength, and was confounding the Yahuḏim who dwelt in Dammeseq, proving that this is ha’Mashiaḥ.
9.23: And after many days had elapsed, the Yahuḏim plotted to kill him.
9.24: But their plot became known to Sha’ul. And they were closely watching the gates day and night, to kill him.
9.25: But taking him by night, the talmidim let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
9.26: And having arrived at Yerushalayim, Sha’ul tried to join the talmidim, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a talmid.
9.27: But Barnaḇah took him and brought him to the emissaries, and told them how he had seen the Aḏon on the way, and that He had spoken to him, and how he was speaking boldly at Dammeseq in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
9.28: And he was with them at Yerushalayim, coming in and going out,
9.29: and speaking boldly in the Name of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and disputed with the Yawanites, but they undertook to kill him.
9.30: And when the brothers learned of this, they brought him down to Kaisereia and sent him out to Tarsos.
9.31: Then indeed the assemblies throughout all Yahuḏah, and Galil, and Shomeron had peace and were built up, and walking in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and in the encouragement of the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, they were being increased.
9.32: And it came to be, as Kĕpha was passing all throughout, that he also came down to the qodeshim who were dwelling at Loḏ.
9.33: And there he found a certain man named Aineas, who had been bedridden for eight years, being paralytic.
9.34: And Kĕpha said to him, “Aineas, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ heals you! Rise up and make your bed.” And immediately he rose up.
9.35: And all those dwelling at Loḏ and Sharon saw him and turned to the Aḏon.
9.36: And in Yapho there was a certain talmid named Taḇitha, which means Dorkas. This woman was filled with good works and kind deeds which she did.
9.37: And it came to be in those days that she became sick and died. And having washed her, they laid her in an upper room.
9.38: And Loḏ being near to Yapho, and the talmidim having heard that Kĕpha was there, they sent two men to him, urging him not to delay in coming to them.
9.39: And having risen up, Kĕpha went with them. And when he arrived, they brought him to the upper room. And all the widows stood beside him weeping, showing the inner garments and outer garments which Dorkas had made while she was with them.
9.40: But Kĕpha sent them all out, and knelt down and prayed. And turning to the body he said, “Taḇitha, arise.” And she opened her eyes, and seeing Kĕpha, she sat up.
9.41: And giving her his hand, he lifted her up. And calling the qodeshim and widows, he presented her alive.
9.42: And it became known throughout all Yapho, and many believed on the Aḏon.
9.43: And it came to be that he stayed for many days in Yapho with Shim’on, a leather-tanner.
